<!--
  This Behavior Tree replans the global path periodically at 1 Hz.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <PipelineSequence name="NavigateWithReplanning">
      <RateController hz="1.0">
        <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
      </RateController>
      <FollowPath path="{path}"  controller_id="FollowPath"/>
    </PipelineSequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a navigation task that periodically replans a global path at 1 Hz while following the latest available path.

The root PipelineSequence NavigateWithReplanning will execute ComputePathToPose and FollowPath in order and will stop if an action fails. It will advance to the next action while the current action is running or has succeeded.

First, the RateController decorator will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose at a rate of 1 Hz. The robot will compute a path to the goal using the GridBased planner and store the path under {path}. It will continue to replan while the path-following action is running.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath using the path stored under {path} and the FollowPath controller.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive goal={goal}, path={path}, and planner_id="GridBased". The ROS action FollowPath will receive path={path} and controller_id="FollowPath".

The mission describes navigation to a goal while replanning the global path after every 1.0 meter.

First, the root PipelineSequence NavigateWithReplanning will execute ComputePathToPose and FollowPath in order and stop if any action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action.

Next, the DistanceController decorator will control ComputePathToPose using a distance interval of 1.0 meter.

Finally, it will execute ROS action ComputePathToPose with the goal read from {goal}. It will store the computed path under {path}. It will use the GridBased planner. It will execute ROS action FollowPath with the path read from {path}. It will use the FollowPath controller.

Parameters: ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive goal="{goal}", path="{path}", and planner_id="GridBased". ROS action FollowPath will receive path="{path}" and controller_id="FollowPath". DistanceController will receive distance="1.0".

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first computes a path using the global planner (ComputePathToPose).
  Then, it runs two sub-branches in parallel. The first sub-branch is a FollowPath
  operation (the local planner). In parallel, there is a rate controlled execution of
  FollowPath (the global planner). Each time a new path is computed, the path update
  is sent to the local planner. The right branch, which is the rate controlled
  ComputePathToPose, always returns RUNNING. Because the Parallel node uses a
  threshold of 1, whenever the FollowPath returns SUCCESS or FAILURE, the parallel
  node will return this result.

  The goal (input to the global planner) and the resulting path (output of the global
  planner and input to the local planner) are passed on the blackboard.

  The rate at which the ComputePathToPose operation is invoked can be controlled with
  the hz parameter to the RateController node.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <RateController hz="1.0">
        <Fallback>
          <GoalReached/>
          <ComputePathToPose goal="${goal}"/>
        </Fallback>
      </RateController>
      <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a navigation task that periodically computes a path to a goal and then follows the resulting path.

First, the root Sequence will execute the RateController subtree and then FollowPath in order. The sequence will stop if either action fails.

Next, the RateController will execute its Fallback subtree at a rate of 1.0 hertz.

Then, the Fallback will execute GoalReached and ComputePathToPose consecutively. If GoalReached fails, it will execute ComputePathToPose. If either action succeeds, the fallback will stop.

Finally, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath after the rate-controlled subtree succeeds.

Parameters: The RateController action will use hz="1.0". The ROS action ComputePathToPose will use goal="${goal}". The ROS action FollowPath will use path="${path}".

The mission describes a fallback-based task in which the robot will enter a known room, find and grasp a bottle, and ask for help if the primary task fails.

First, the root node will execute FB1 and use Ask_for_help if FB1 fails.

Next, FB1 will execute S1 and use Ask_for_help if S1 fails.

Then, S1 will execute FB2 followed by S2 in order and will stop if either subtree fails.

Next, FB2 will execute S7 and use FollowHuman if S7 fails.

Then, S7 will check Room_known and will stop if the condition fails.

Next, FB10 will check Robot_in_room and will execute Go_to_room if the condition is false.

Then, S2 will execute FB3 followed by FB4 in order and will stop if either subtree fails.

Next, FB3 will check Bottle_found and will execute Find_bottle if the condition is false.

Then, FB4 will check Bottle_grasped and will execute FB5 if the condition is false.

Next, FB5 will execute S3 and will execute FB6 if S3 fails.

Then, S3 will execute FB7 followed by S4 in order and will stop if either subtree fails.

Next, FB7 will execute S6 and will execute Compute_inv_pose if S6 fails.

Then, S6 will check Inv_pose_computed and Inv_pose_valid in order and will stop if either condition fails.

Next, S4 will execute FB8 followed by S5 in order and will stop if either subtree fails.

Then, FB8 will check Robot_at_inv_pose and will execute S8 if the condition is false.

Next, S8 will execute Keep_arms_for_grasp followed by Go_to_inv_pose in order and will stop if either action fails.

Then, S5 will execute FB9 followed by Grasp_bottle in order and will stop if either subtree or action fails.

Next, FB9 will check Bottle_located and will execute Locate_bottle if the condition is false.

Finally, FB6 will execute Set_inv_pose_not_valid and will use Keep_running if the first action fails.

Parameters: No actions in this behavior tree define ports.

First, the root node will execute the fallback FB1 consecutively. If any child action fails, it will move to the next child until one succeeds. If no child succeeds, the execution will fail.

Next, fallback FB1 will first execute sequence S1. If sequence S1 fails, it will execute custom action Ask_for_help. If custom action Ask_for_help fails, the fallback will fail.

Next, sequence S1 will execute fallback FB2 followed by sequence S2 in order. The sequence will stop if either child fails.

Next, sequence S3 will execute custom action Fetch_bottle followed by sequence S4. The sequence will stop if either child fails.

Next, sequence S4 will execute custom action Find_glass followed by sequence S5. The sequence will stop if either child fails.

Finally, sequence S5 will execute custom action Fetch_glass followed by custom action Pour_drink. The sequence will stop if either action fails.

First, the root ReactiveSequence will execute AIP_isHolding, AIP_isAt, and AIP_isPlacedAt in sequence. If any action fails, it will stop execution. Next, it will run the custom action AIP_isHolding with the specified holding-state goal.

Finally, it will run the custom action AIP_isPlacedAt with the specified placement-state goal after AIP_isAt succeeds.

mrq:
The mission describes a repeated item-pursuit task that checks for an item, picks it up when necessary, and places it when the gripper holds an item.

First, the root Repeat node will execute the Pursue Goals sequence continuously because its cycle limit is -1.

Next, the Pursue Goals sequence will execute the No Item to pick fallback followed by the No Item in gripper fallback in order and stop if either fallback fails.

Next, the No Item to pick fallback will execute its children consecutively. It will first execute the inverted Not decorator. If the SeeItem condition succeeds, the decorator will fail. If the SeeItem condition fails, the decorator will succeed. If the decorator fails, it will execute the Pick action. If neither child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, the No Item in gripper fallback will execute its children consecutively. It will first execute the inverted Not decorator. If the HoldingItem condition succeeds, the decorator will fail. If the HoldingItem condition fails, the decorator will succeed. If the decorator fails, it will execute the Place action. If neither child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Parameters: The Pick action has no ports. The Place action has no ports.

mrq:
The mission describes passing through an opening by using an already open door, opening a closed door when necessary, or passing through a window as a fallback.

First, the root fallback root_Fallback will execute door_open_sequence, DoorClosed, and PassThroughWindow consecutively. If any action in the fallback succeeds, it will stop execution. If all actions fail, the mission will fail.

Next, the sequence door_open_sequence will execute IsDoorOpen and PassThroughDoor in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. It will check whether the door is open. If the door is open, it will pass through the door.

Next, the DoorClosed subtree will execute door_closed_sequence. The sequence door_closed_sequence will execute the inverted IsDoorOpen check, OpenDoor with up to four attempts, PassThroughDoor, and CloseDoor in order and stop if any action fails. It will execute the inverted IsDoorOpen check. If IsDoorOpen succeeds, the inverted check will fail. If IsDoorOpen fails, the inverted check will succeed. It will keep trying to execute OpenDoor until it succeeds, with no more than four attempts. After the door opens, it will pass through the door. After passing through the door, it will close the door.

Finally, it will pass through the window if the open-door sequence and the DoorClosed subtree both fail.

Parameters: The OpenDoor action will use num_attempts="4".

mrq:
The mission describes navigation to a goal with periodic path replanning and recovery actions.

First, the root recovery node will execute the main navigation pipeline. If the pipeline fails, it will execute the recovery fallback and retry the main pipeline until the retry limit is exhausted.

Next, the pipeline sequence will execute the rate-controlled path computation and path following in order. It will advance to path following while path computation is running or has succeeded. It will stop if either recovery node fails.

Next, the rate controller will run the path-computation recovery node at a frequency of 1.0 Hz.

Next, the path-computation recovery node will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose. If path computation fails, it will execute the custom action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context and retry path computation. It will stop after one recovery retry is exhausted.

Next, the robot will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose with the goal from the blackboard and store the resulting path on the blackboard.

Next, the path-following recovery node will execute the ROS action FollowPath. If path following fails, it will execute the custom action ClearLocalCostmap-Context and retry path following. It will stop after one recovery retry is exhausted.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath using the stored path.

Next, the recovery fallback will execute GoalUpdated before the recovery action sequence. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop recovery processing. If GoalUpdated fails, it will execute the recovery action sequence.

Next, the recovery action sequence will execute its actions in order. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from the failed action.

Next, it will execute the custom action ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree. It will then execute the custom action ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree. It will then execute the ROS action Spin. It will finally execute the ROS action Wait.

The custom action ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap". The ROS action Spin will use spin_dist="1.57". The mission describes obtaining a job and repeatedly attempting the available job procedures until one succeeds.

First, the root node will execute the Jobs subtree.

Next, the Jobs sequence will execute GetJob and then the FallbackStar containing JobButcherAnimal, JobDyeAnimal, JobLeadAnimalToPasture, JobHarvestAnimal, JobTameAnimal, JobHaulMultiple, and JobStandard. If a job procedure fails, it will try the next procedure. If every procedure fails, it will restart from JobButcherAnimal.

Next, the JobButcherAnimal precondition will check whether the blackboard value for JobType matches ButcherAnimal. If the check passes, its fallback will try the butcher sequence and then AbortJob if that sequence fails. The butcher sequence will initialize the animal job, move, grab the animal, get the item drop position, move, perform the final animal movement, butcher the animal, and finish the job in sequence. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the JobDyeAnimal precondition will check whether the blackboard value for JobType matches DyeAnimal. If the check passes, its fallback will try the dye sequence and then AbortJob if that sequence fails. The dye sequence will initialize the job, claim items, move all items to the job, initialize the animal job, move, grab the animal, get the item drop position, move, perform the final animal movement, dye the animal, and finish the job in sequence. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the JobLeadAnimalToPasture precondition will check whether the blackboard value for JobType matches LeadAnimalToPasture. If the check passes, its fallback will try the leading sequence and then AbortJob if that sequence fails. The leading sequence will initialize the animal job, move, grab the animal, get the item drop position, move, perform the final animal movement, release the animal, and finish the job in sequence. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the JobHarvestAnimal precondition will check whether the blackboard value for JobType matches HarvestAnimal. If the check passes, its fallback will try the harvesting sequence and then AbortJob if that sequence fails. The harvesting sequence will initialize the animal job, move, grab the animal, harvest the animal, release the animal, and finish the job in sequence. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the JobTameAnimal precondition will check whether the blackboard value for JobType matches TameAnimal. If the check passes, its fallback will try the taming sequence and then AbortJob if that sequence fails. The taming sequence will initialize the animal job, move, tame the animal, grab the animal, get the item drop position, move, perform the final animal movement, release the animal, and finish the job in sequence. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the JobHaulMultiple precondition will check whether the blackboard value for JobType matches HauleMultipleItems. If the check passes, its fallback will try the hauling sequence and then AbortJob if that sequence fails. The hauling sequence will initialize the job, find a tool, move, and equip the tool. The inverter will execute its child with inverted results. Its child will execute another inverter, a pickup sequence, and ReturnAlwaysRunning in order and will reverse the resulting status. The inner inverter will reverse the result of checking whether AllPickedUp is true. The pickup sequence will move and pick up an item. The outer sequence will stop if any action fails. The hauling sequence will then check AllPickedUp, get the item drop position, move, drop all items, and finish the job. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the JobStandard fallback will try the StandardJobs sequence and then AbortJob if the sequence fails. The StandardJobs sequence will initialize the job, claim items, find a tool, move, equip the tool, move all items to the job, get the work position, move, work, and finish the job in sequence. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the MoveAllItemsToJob sequence will execute its inverted item-moving procedure and then check AllItemsInPlaceForJob. The inverted procedure will execute an inner inverter, the item-moving sequence, and ReturnAlwaysRunning in order and will reverse the resulting status. The inner inverter will reverse the result of checking whether AllItemsInPlaceForJob is true. The item-moving sequence will move, pick up an item, get the item drop position, move, and drop the item. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the GetUniform SequenceStar named GetUniform will execute CheckUniform, the uniform fallback, and EquipUniform in sequence. The uniform fallback will try Move and then UniformCleanUp if Move fails. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the Combat SequenceStar will check IsInCombat, abort the job, execute the forced-success combat procedure, and check IsInCombat again. The forced-success node will execute its child and make sure it always succeeds. Its child SequenceStar will get a target, move, and execute the adjacent-target sequence. The adjacent-target sequence will check TargetAdjacent and attack the target in order. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the Hunger SequenceStar will check IsHungry and execute the hunger sequence with a fullness check. The hunger sequence will find food, move, pick up an item, execute the forced-success dining procedure, and eat. The forced-success node will execute its child and make sure it always succeeds. Its child SequenceStar will find dining and move. The outer sequence will then check IsFull. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the Sleep SequenceStar named Sleep will check IsSleepy, execute the forced-success bed-finding procedure, and sleep. The forced-success node will execute its child and make sure it always succeeds. Its child SequenceStar will find a bed and move. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the Thirst SequenceStar will check IsThirsty and execute the thirst sequence with a drink-full check. The thirst sequence will find a drink, move, pick up an item, execute the forced-success dining procedure, and drink. The forced-success node will execute its child and make sure it always succeeds. Its child SequenceStar will find dining and move. The outer sequence will then check IsDrinkFull. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the Trainer SequenceStar named Trainer will check IsTrainer, find the trainer position, move, and supervise training. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

Next, the Training SequenceStar named Training will check IsTrainingTime, find the training ground, move, and train. The SequenceStar will remember successful actions and restart from the failed action when an action fails.

The mission describes a repeated interactive game routine that initializes pose detection, tracks a person, localizes the robot, optionally sets up game positions, and then conducts the game.

First, the root Repeat node will execute its child sequence 10 times.

Next, the Sequence node will execute Delay, TrackAction, two RobotSpin actions, RobotFindInitAction, and Fallback in order. It will stop the sequence if any child action fails.

Next, the Delay node will wait for its delay timer before executing PoseDetectionControlAction. The robot will enable pose detection after the delay period.

Next, it will execute TrackAction to track a person at rate 3 without voice detection or base turning.

Next, it will execute RobotSpin with an angle of -180 degrees and velocity 0.4. It will then execute RobotSpin with an angle of 180 degrees and velocity 0.4.

Next, it will execute RobotFindInitAction using the game file robot_find.json for shapes in fixed order. It will store the initialization requirement under {needs_init} and the robot pose under {robot_pose}.

Next, the Fallback node will execute its child actions consecutively. If a child fails, it will move to the next child until one succeeds. If no child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, the BlackboardCheckInt node will check whether {needs_init} matches 1. If the values do not match, this branch will fail.

Next, the setup Sequence node will execute its actions in order and stop if any action fails. It will track the person with base turning enabled. It will announce the game setup instructions.

Next, the ForceSuccess node will execute its child Sequence and make sure it always succeeds. The child Sequence will ask the person to stand in the middle, repeatedly wait two seconds for both hands to be detected on the hips for up to 20 attempts, and then track the person without base turning.

Next, the second ForceSuccess node will execute KeepRunningUntilFailure and make sure it always succeeds. KeepRunningUntilFailure will execute its child Sequence and restart it whenever the sequence succeeds. It will stop looping when the sequence fails.

Next, the child Sequence will find the next game position, announce that position, and repeatedly wait two seconds for both hands to be detected on the hips, obtain the object's location, and set the robot position using that location. The retry operation will allow up to 20 attempts.

Next, it will announce that setup is finished and track the person without base turning.

Next, the gameplay Sequence will execute Nav2Client, TextToSpeechActionClient, TrackAction, ForceSuccess, TextToSpeechActionClient, and TrackAction in order. It will stop if any action outside ForceSuccess fails.

Next, it will execute Nav2Client using {robot_pose} as the navigation goal.

Next, it will announce that the game is starting and track the person at rate 3 without voice detection or base turning.

Next, the ForceSuccess node will execute KeepRunningUntilFailure and make sure it always succeeds. KeepRunningUntilFailure will repeatedly execute its child Sequence until that sequence fails.

Next, the child Sequence will find the next game position and announce where the person should stand. It will repeatedly wait one second, obtain the object's location, check whether the person is at that location, and announce “Good job.” The retry operation will allow up to 200 attempts.

Next, it will announce that the game is finished and track the person at rate 3 without voice detection or base turning.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first goes into a branch where it will check to see if the robot's initial
  pose is given. If the initial pose is not given it trys to automatically localize the robot.
  After finding the initial pose it will continue with the recovery and navigation branch.  The
  AutoLocalization branch is based on 'AutoLocalization.xml' and the navigation branch is based on
  `parallel_w_recovery.xml`.
-->
<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <FallbackStar name="AutoLocalization">
        <initialPoseReceived/>
        <SequenceStar name="doSelfLocalization">
          <RetryUntilSuccesful num_attempts="5" name="retry_client_request">
            <globalLocalizationServiceRequest/>
         </RetryUntilSuccesful>
         <RetryUntilSuccesful num_attempts="10" name="retry_localization">
            <Sequence>
              <Fallback>
                <IsLocalized/>
                <SequenceStar>
                 <Spin/>
                <BackUp/>
                 <Spin/>
              </SequenceStar>
             </Fallback>
             <IsLocalized/>
            </Sequence> 
          </RetryUntilSuccesful>
        </SequenceStar>
      </FallbackStar>
      <FallbackStar name="check_motion">
        <Inverter name="is_not_stuck">
          <IsStuck/>
        </Inverter>
        <SequenceStar name="stuck_recovery">
          <Stop/>
          <BackUp/>
          <Spin/>
        </SequenceStar>
      </FallbackStar>
      <SequenceStar name="navigate">
        <ComputePathToPose endpoints="${endpoints}" path="${path}"/>
        <ParallelNode threshold="1">
          <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
          <Sequence>
            <RateController hz="2">
              <ComputePathToPose endpoints="${endpoints}" path="${path}"/>
            </RateController>
            <UpdatePath/>
          </Sequence>
        </ParallelNode>
      </SequenceStar>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a localization, recovery, and navigation task.

First, the root sequence will execute AutoLocalization, check_motion, and navigate in order. The sequence will stop if any child action fails.

Next, AutoLocalization will execute its child actions consecutively. If any child action fails, it will restart from the beginning until one action succeeds. It will check whether the initial pose has been received. If the initial pose has not been received, it will execute doSelfLocalization.

Then, doSelfLocalization will execute retry_client_request and retry_localization in sequence. If either action succeeds, it will remember that action and continue to the next action. If either action fails, it will restart from the failed action.

Next, retry_client_request will keep trying to execute globalLocalizationServiceRequest until it succeeds.

Then, retry_localization will keep trying to execute its sequence until it succeeds. The sequence will execute the fallback and IsLocalized actions in order and will stop if an action fails.

Next, the fallback will execute IsLocalized and the unnamed SequenceStar consecutively. If IsLocalized fails, it will execute the unnamed SequenceStar. If no child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Then, the unnamed SequenceStar will execute Spin, BackUp, and Spin in sequence. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from that action.

Next, check_motion will execute its child actions consecutively. If any child action fails, it will restart from the beginning until one action succeeds. It will execute inverted is_not_stuck. If is_not_stuck succeeds, it will reverse the result to failure. If is_not_stuck fails, it will reverse the result to success.

Then, is_not_stuck will execute IsStuck with its result inverted. If IsStuck succeeds, the decorator will fail. If IsStuck fails, the decorator will succeed.

Next, stuck_recovery will execute Stop, BackUp, and Spin in sequence. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from that action.

Finally, navigate will execute ComputePathToPose and the ParallelNode in sequence. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from that action.

Next, the ParallelNode will execute FollowPath and its second Sequence simultaneously. If at least one action succeeds, the parallel execution will succeed. If any action fails, the parallel execution will fail.

Then, the second Sequence will execute RateController and UpdatePath in order and will stop if any action fails. While RateController is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to UpdatePath.

Parameters: The ROS action globalLocalizationServiceRequest will use no ports. The ROS action ComputePathToPose will read endpoints from {endpoints} and store the path under {path}. The ROS action FollowPath will read the path from {path}. The ROS action RateController will use hz="2". The ROS action ComputePathToPose will read endpoints from {endpoints} and store the path under {path}. The ParallelNode will use threshold="1".

<!--
  This Behavior Tree processes each of the given waypoints with NavigateToPose and wait if NavigateToPose is failed.

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <ReactiveFallback name="FollowWaypoints">
      <AllGoalsAchieved goal_achieved="{goal_achieved}"/>
      <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
        <ReactiveSequence>
          <GetNextGoal goals="{goals}" goal="{goal}" goal_achieved="{goal_achieved}"/>
          <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1">
            <NavigateToPose goal="{goal}"/>
            <Wait wait_duration="5"/>
          </RecoveryNode>
          <SetBlackboard output_key="goal_achieved" value="true"/>
        </ReactiveSequence>
      </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    </ReactiveFallback>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes processing each waypoint by navigating to it and waiting after navigation failure.

First, the root ReactiveFallback named FollowWaypoints will execute AllGoalsAchieved and then the KeepRunningUntilFailure subtree in order. If AllGoalsAchieved succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will continue executing and re-evaluating AllGoalsAchieved while the later subtree is running. If AllGoalsAchieved becomes true, it will halt the running subtree and stop the fallback.

Next, the AllGoalsAchieved condition will check whether {goal_achieved} indicates that all goals have been achieved.

Then, the KeepRunningUntilFailure node will execute the ReactiveSequence. If the ReactiveSequence succeeds, it will restart it. If the ReactiveSequence fails, it will stop looping and continue execution.

After that, the ReactiveSequence will execute GetNextGoal, the RecoveryNode, and SetBlackboard in sequence. If any action fails, it will stop the sequence. While an action is running, it will re-evaluate previous actions and halt the running action if a previous action fails.

Next, GetNextGoal will obtain the next goal from {goals}, store it in {goal}, and use {goal_achieved} to track whether goal processing is complete.

Then, the RecoveryNode will execute NavigateToPose as its main action. If navigation fails, it will execute Wait as the recovery action. After recovery, it will retry NavigateToPose. If recovery fails and the retry limit is exhausted, it will stop execution.

Finally, SetBlackboard will store true under {goal_achieved} after the navigation and recovery sequence succeeds.

Parameters: NavigateToPose will use goal="{goal}". GetNextGoal will use goals="{goals}", goal="{goal}", and goal_achieved="{goal_achieved}". SetBlackboard will use output_key="goal_achieved" and value="true". Wait will use wait_duration="5". RecoveryNode will use number_of_retries="1".

First, the root Repeat node will execute its child {num_cycles} times.

Next, the Sequence node will execute the pre-check and reactive execution in order, and it will stop if either action fails. It will then update the logical-task state after the reactive execution succeeds.

Next, the Fallback node will execute LTLPreCheck. If LTLPreCheck fails, it will execute ReplanningRequestLevel2 through ForceFailure, which will make that branch fail.

Next, the ForceFailure node will execute ReplanningRequestLevel2 and make sure it always fails.

Next, the ReactiveSequence node will execute its four child branches in order. If a branch fails, it will stop execution. While a later branch is running, it will re-evaluate preceding branches and halt the running branch if a preceding branch fails.

Next, the Fallback node will first execute the locomotion and level-one detection sequence. If that sequence fails, it will execute ReplanningRequestLevel1 through ForceFailure.

Next, the Sequence node will execute the locomotion recovery and FakeDetectionLevel1 in order, and it will stop if either action fails.

Next, the RetryUntilSuccesful node will keep trying its child up to three attempts until it succeeds.

Next, the Fallback node will check LocomotionStatusCheck. If that check fails, it will execute RecoveryStand and then delayed LocomotionStart.

Next, the Delay node will wait 2000 milliseconds before executing LocomotionStart.

Next, the Fallback node will check ReactiveLTLStateCheck. If that check fails, it will execute ReplanningRequestLevel2 through ForceFailure.

Next, the Fallback node will execute FakeDetectionLevel3. If that action fails, it will execute ReplanningRequestLevel3 through ForceFailure.

Next, the Fallback node will read {bt_action_type} and compare it with the cases move, stay, pick, drop, start_training, and terminate_training. It will execute the corresponding action when a case matches. If no case matches, it will execute AlwaysFailure and then try ReplanningRequestLevel3 through ForceFailure.

Next, the Switch6 node will execute MoveAction for move, StayAction for stay, PickAction for pick, DropAction for drop, GuideAction for start_training, and BackNormalAction for terminate_training.

Next, the ForceFailure node will execute ReplanningRequestLevel3 and make sure it always fails.

Finally, the robot will execute UpdateLTL to update the action sequence, executed action sequence, action type, current action, and desired logical-task sequence.

TruncatePath will read {path} from input_path, store the shortened path under {truncated_path} in output_path, and use 1.0 as distance. FollowPath will read {truncated_path} from path and use FollowPath as controller_id.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first goes into a branch where it will check if the robot is stuck.
  If that is the case, it will attempt to recover. Otherwise it will continue with
  the navigation branch. In this case the navigation branch is based on `simple_sequential.xml`.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <FallbackStar name="check_motion">
        <Inverter name="is_not_stuck">
          <IsStuck/>
        </Inverter>
        <SequenceStar name="stuck_recovery">
          <Stop/>
          <BackUp/>
          <Spin/>
        </SequenceStar>
      </FallbackStar>
      <SequenceStar name="navigate">
        <ComputePathToPose endpoints="${endpoints}" path="${path}"/>
        <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
      </SequenceStar>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The mission describes a navigation task that checks for a stuck condition, performs recovery when necessary, and then follows a computed path.

First, the root Sequence named root will execute check_motion followed by navigate in order and will stop if either action fails.

Next, the FallbackStar named check_motion will execute is_not_stuck followed by stuck_recovery. If an action fails, it will move to the next action until one succeeds. If all actions fail, it will restart from is_not_stuck until one succeeds.

The Inverter named is_not_stuck will execute inverted IsStuck. If IsStuck succeeds, it will reverse the result to failure. If IsStuck fails, it will reverse the result to success.

The SequenceStar named stuck_recovery will execute Stop, BackUp, and Spin in sequence. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from the failed action.

Finally, the SequenceStar named navigate will execute ComputePathToPose followed by FollowPath in sequence. If ComputePathToPose succeeds, it will remember the action and move to FollowPath. If an action fails, it will restart from the failed action.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive endpoints from {endpoints} and store the computed path under {path}. The ROS action FollowPath will receive the path from {path}.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first computes a path using the global planner (ComputePathToPose).
  Then, it runs two sub-branches in parallel. The first sub-branch is a FollowPath
  operation (the local planner). In parallel, there is a rate controlled execution of
  FollowPath (the global planner). Each time a new path is computed, the path update
  is sent to the local planner. The right branch, which is the rate controlled
  ComputePathToPose, always returns RUNNING. Because the Parallel node uses a
  threshold of 1, whenever the FollowPath returns SUCCESS or FAILURE, the parallel
  node will return this result.

  The goal (input to the global planner) and the resulting path (output of the global
  planner and input to the local planner) are passed on the blackboard.

  The rate at which the ComputePathToPose operation is invoked can be controlled with
  the hz parameter to the RateController node.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <RateController hz="1.0">
        <Fallback>
          <GoalReached/>
          <ComputePathToPose goal="${goal}"/>
        </Fallback>
      </RateController>
      <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Next, the first root sequence will execute checkMissionWait and stop in order. The sequence will stop if either child fails. The robot will check whether checkMissionWait is true. It will run stop when that condition succeeds.

Next, the second root sequence will execute init, genGlobalFollowPath, mission_start, and setPath in order. The sequence will stop if any action fails. It will run init before generating a global follow path. It will execute the fallback named mission_start before setting the path.

Next, mission_start will execute its child sequences consecutively. If a child sequence fails, it will move to the next child until one succeeds. If no child succeeds, it will execute drive.

Next, the first mission_start sequence will check checkFrontObject. It will continue only when checkFrontObject is true. It will execute the nested fallback for front-object handling.

Next, the front-object fallback will first execute the global-follow sequence. If that sequence fails, it will execute the lane-check fallback.

Next, the global-follow sequence will check checkIsGlobalFollow. If that condition is true, it will execute loc_check. If the condition is false, the sequence will fail.

Next, loc_check will try the near-corner sequence, the near-stopline sequence, and the keep-lane sequence in order. If a condition fails, it will try the next sequence. If all conditions fail, loc_check will fail.

Next, the near-corner sequence will check checkNearCorner and run acc when the condition is true. The near-stopline sequence will check checkNearStopline and run acc when the condition is true. The keep-lane sequence will check checkProfitKeeplane and run acc when the condition is true.

Next, lane_check will first check checkLaneChange. If that condition is true, it will execute the nested lane-check fallback. If the condition is false, it will execute Local_path.

Next, the nested lane-check fallback will first check checkLeftchageAble. If that condition is true, it will try to keep the lane when checkCollision is true and otherwise change left. If checkLeftchageAble is false, it will try to keep the lane when checkCollision is true and otherwise change right.

Next, Local_path will execute its local-path generation sequence and local-check fallback in order. The sequence will stop if either subtree fails.

Next, the local-path generation sequence will check checkEmptyLocal. If that condition is true, it will stop, generate a local path, and set the local start. If the condition is false, it will skip local-path generation.

Next, local_check will try the finish-local sequence, the collision-stop sequence, and localPathfollow in order. If checkFinishLocal is true, it will run setFinishLocal. If that sequence fails, it will check checkCollision and run stop when the condition is true. If both sequences fail, it will run localPathfollow.

Next, the second mission_start sequence will check checkNearStopline. If that condition is true, it will execute the passability fallback. If the condition is false, the sequence will fail.

Next, the passability fallback will check checkPassAble. If that condition is true, it will execute the collision-and-drive sequence. If the condition is false, it will run stop.

Next, the collision-and-drive sequence will check checkCollision and run stop when the condition is true. It will then run drive if the preceding action succeeds.

Next, the standalone drive action will run when the earlier mission_start children fail and the fallback reaches its final child.

First, the root Repeat node will execute the Sequence subtree one time.

Next, the Sequence node will execute the following actions (LookAtTheTray, RetryUntilSuccessful, PickTray, LookUp, MoveBack, GoToTable, PlaceTray) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, it will execute custom action LookAtTheTray.

Next, the RetryUntilSuccessful node will keep trying to execute the Timeout subtree until it succeeds.

Next, the Timeout node will execute custom action DetectHandles for a maximum of 300 milliseconds. If DetectHandles fails to execute within 300 milliseconds, it will interrupt the execution and stop it.

Next, it will execute custom action PickTray.

Next, it will execute custom action LookUp.

Next, it will execute custom action MoveBack.

Next, it will execute custom action GoToTable.

Finally, it will execute custom action PlaceTray.

Next, the SequenceStar named Retreat will execute IsDay, FindRetreat, Move, and the nested sleep sequence in order. It will execute custom action FindRetreat. It will execute custom action Move. It will execute the nested Sequence.

Next, the nested Sequence will execute IsDay and Sleep in order. It will stop if either action fails. It will check whether IsDay is true. It will execute custom action Sleep after IsDay succeeds.

The mission describes a repeated locomotion task that checks the LTL state, prepares locomotion, performs movement, and updates the LTL plan.

First, the root Repeat node will execute the Sequence {num_cycles} times.

Next, the Sequence will execute the following actions (the first Fallback, the ReactiveSequence, UpdateLTL) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

Then, the first Fallback will execute its child actions consecutively. If LTLPreCheck fails, it will execute ForceFailure. If no child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

It will execute custom action LTLPreCheck using the current LTL state and the desired LTL state sequence. If LTLPreCheck fails, ForceFailure will execute custom action Replanning2 and make sure it always fails.

Next, the ReactiveSequence will execute the following actions (the second Fallback, the third Fallback) in sequence. If the second Fallback fails, it will stop execution. While the third Fallback is running, it will re-evaluate the second Fallback; if the second Fallback fails, it will halt the running third Fallback and stop the sequence.

Then, the second Fallback will execute its child actions consecutively. If LocomotionStatusCheck fails, it will move to Timeout. If Timeout fails, it will move to ForceFailure. If no child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

It will execute custom action LocomotionStatusCheck.

It will execute delayed Sequence after the delay timer. After the delay period is exhausted, it will resume execution.

The delayed Sequence will execute the following actions (RecoveryStand, LocomotionStart) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

It will execute custom action RecoveryStand. It will execute custom action LocomotionStart after RecoveryStand succeeds.

If the delayed Sequence fails, ForceFailure will execute custom action Replanning3 and make sure it always fails.

Next, the third Fallback will execute its child actions consecutively. If MoveAction fails, it will execute ForceFailure. If no child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

It will execute custom action MoveAction using the navigation goal, the locomotion completion status, and the locomotion idle status. If MoveAction fails, ForceFailure will execute custom action Replanning3 and make sure it always fails.

Finally, custom action UpdateLTL will execute after the ReactiveSequence succeeds.

Custom action MoveAction will store its action result in {action} and read {move_base_finished}, {move_base_idle}, and {nav_goal}. Custom action UpdateLTL will read and update {action_sequence}, update {ltl_state_desired_sequence}, and store the navigation goal in {nav_goal}. The Repeat node will use {num_cycles} as its cycle count. The Timeout node has an empty msec value.

The mission describes an automated coffee-machine operation that opens the machine, completes cleaning requirements, places a coffee cup, selects coffee settings, dispenses coffee, and performs post-dispensing actions.

First, the root sequence will execute the following actions in order and stop if any action fails: OpenCoffeMachine, AutoClean, PutCoffeCup, and CoffeType.

Next, the OpenCoffeMachine fallback will check whether the machine is open. If the machine is open, this subtree will succeed. If the machine is not open, it will execute the sequence that waits for a clean cup and switches on the machine.

The sequence will execute RetryUntilSuccesful and the second fallback in order and stop if either action fails. RetryUntilSuccesful will keep checking whether a clean cup is ready until the check succeeds, for up to 10 attempts. The fallback will first wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the machine to be open. If the machine does not open within that time, it will switch on the coffee machine.

Next, the AutoClean fallback will check whether the cleaning process is finished. If the cleaning process is finished, this subtree will succeed. If it is not finished, the fallback will execute the water-management fallback and then the marro-management fallback.

The water-management fallback will first check whether there is enough water. If enough water is available, it will succeed. If enough water is unavailable, it will execute the water-management sequence.

The water-management sequence will wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the water tank to be removed. It will then wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the water tank to be full. If the tank is not full within that time, it will fill the water tank. It will then retry checking whether the water tank is placed in the coffee machine until the check succeeds, for up to 100 attempts.

The marro-management fallback will execute the inverted check for whether the marro tank is full. If the marro tank is not full, the inverted check will succeed. If the marro tank is full, it will execute the marro-management sequence.

The marro-management sequence will wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the marro tank to be removed. It will then wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the marro tank to be empty. If the tank is not empty within that time, it will empty the marro tank. It will then retry checking whether the marro tank is placed in the coffee machine until the check succeeds, for up to 100 attempts.

Next, the PutCoffeCup fallback will wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the coffee cup to be ready. If the cup is not ready within that time, it will place the coffee cup.

Finally, the CoffeType sequence will execute the following actions in order and stop if any action fails: the coffee-selection fallback, the coffee-finished check, the cup-removal check, the cleaning-cup fallback, and the milk-and-sugar fallback.

The coffee-selection fallback will wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the desired coffee to be selected. If the desired coffee is not selected within that time, it will press the desired coffee control.

The sequence will wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the coffee to finish.

The sequence will wait up to 5000 milliseconds for the coffee cup to be removed.

The cleaning-cup fallback will first check whether a human has added the cleaning cup. If the cleaning cup has not been added, it will place a clean cup and switch off the coffee machine.

The milk-and-sugar fallback will first check whether a human has added milk. If milk has not been added, it will execute the milk-and-sugar sequence.

The milk-and-sugar sequence will add milk if milk is desired and will add sugar if sugar is desired.

The inverted milk check will succeed when milk is not desired and will fail when milk is desired.

The inverted sugar check will succeed when sugar is not desired and will fail when sugar is desired.

Parameters: RetryUntilSuccesful in OpenCoffeMachine will use num_attempts="10". RetryUntilSuccesful in AutoClean will use num_attempts="100". All Timeout nodes will use msec="5000".

The mission describes navigation to a goal with periodic path replanning and recovery actions.

First, the root recovery node NavigateRecovery will execute the main navigation pipeline. If the main pipeline fails, it will execute the recovery action and retry the main pipeline until two recovery attempts are exhausted.

Next, the pipeline sequence NavigateWithReplanning will execute RateController and FollowPath in order and will stop if either action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action.

Next, the rate controller will execute the ComputePathToPose recovery node at a rate of 1 Hz.

Next, the ComputePathToPose recovery node will execute the path computation action. If path computation fails, it will execute PathToPoseFallback and retry path computation up to four times.

Next, the PathToPoseFallback reactive fallback will execute GoalUpdated and then GlobalPlannerRecoveryActions in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will continue evaluating the recovery actions and will stop when one succeeds.

Next, the global planner recovery actions will execute ClearGlobalCostmap-Context and Wait consecutively. If ClearGlobalCostmap-Context fails, they will execute Wait. If all recovery actions fail, they will retry from the beginning.

Next, the FollowPath recovery node will execute the path-following action using the computed path. If path following fails, it will execute FollowPathFallback and retry path following up to four times.

Next, the FollowPathFallback reactive fallback will execute GoalUpdated and then PlannerRecoveryActions in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will continue evaluating the recovery actions and will stop when one succeeds.

Next, the planner recovery actions will execute ClearLocalCostmap-Context and Spin consecutively. If ClearLocalCostmap-Context fails, they will execute Spin. If all recovery actions fail, they will retry from the beginning.

Finally, the RecoveryFallback reactive fallback will execute GoalUpdated and then Wait in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will execute Wait and re-evaluate GoalUpdated while Wait is running.

The mission describes continuously navigating through an array of poses while periodically replanning the global path and applying planning, control, and system recovery actions.

First, the root recovery node NavigateRecovery will execute the main navigation pipeline. If the main pipeline fails, it will execute the recovery fallback and retry the main pipeline until six recovery attempts are exhausted.

Next, the pipeline sequence NavigateWithReplanning will execute RateController and FollowPath in order and will stop if either action fails. While RateController is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to FollowPath.

Next, RateController will execute ComputePathThroughPoses after each rate interval at 0.333 Hz.

Next, the recovery node ComputePathThroughPoses will execute its main reactive sequence. If the main sequence fails, it will execute its recovery fallback and retry the main sequence once.

Next, the reactive sequence will execute RemovePassedGoals and ComputePathThroughPoses in sequence. If RemovePassedGoals fails, it will stop the sequence. While ComputePathThroughPoses is running, it will re-evaluate RemovePassedGoals and will stop if that action fails.

Next, it will execute the custom action RemovePassedGoals to remove passed goals within a radius of 0.7 meters.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ComputePathThroughPoses to compute a path through the remaining goals.

Next, the reactive fallback ComputePathThroughPosesRecoveryFallback will execute GoalUpdated and ClearGlobalCostmap-Context in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. If GoalUpdated fails, it will execute ClearGlobalCostmap-Context. While ClearGlobalCostmap-Context is running, it will re-evaluate GoalUpdated and will stop the clearing action if GoalUpdated succeeds.

Next, it will execute the custom action GoalUpdated to check whether the goal has changed.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context to clear the global costmap.

Next, the recovery node FollowPath will execute its main action. If the main action fails, it will execute its recovery fallback and retry the main action once.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath using the computed path.

Next, the reactive fallback FollowPathRecoveryFallback will execute GoalUpdated and ClearLocalCostmap-Context in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. If GoalUpdated fails, it will execute ClearLocalCostmap-Context. While ClearLocalCostmap-Context is running, it will re-evaluate GoalUpdated and will stop the clearing action if GoalUpdated succeeds.

Next, it will execute the custom action GoalUpdated to check whether the goal has changed.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ClearLocalCostmap-Context to clear the local costmap.

Finally, the reactive fallback RecoveryFallback will execute GoalUpdated and RecoveryActions in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. If GoalUpdated fails, it will execute RecoveryActions. While RecoveryActions is running, it will re-evaluate GoalUpdated and will stop the recovery actions if GoalUpdated succeeds.

Finally, the round-robin node RecoveryActions will execute its recovery children in rotation.

Finally, the sequence ClearingActions will execute ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree and ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree in order and will stop if either action fails.

Finally, it will execute the ROS action ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree to clear the local costmap.

Finally, it will execute the ROS action ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree to clear the global costmap.

The mission describes a reactive service mission that monitors mission completion, manages battery status, selects tasks, and returns to or operates from designated stations.

First, the root reactive fallback will execute the mission-over sequence and then the continuously running mission fallback in order. If the mission-over sequence succeeds, it will stop execution. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate earlier actions and stop the running action if an earlier action succeeds. The robot will check whether the mission is over and will return to the station if the mission is over. It will force the mission fallback to remain running.

Next, the mission fallback will execute the battery-sufficient sequence and then the recharge fallback in order. If an action succeeds, it will stop execution. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate earlier actions and stop the running action if an earlier action succeeds. It will check whether the battery is sufficient. It will execute the drop-tool subtree with forced failure. It will invert the result of the idle action. If the inverted idle action succeeds, it will execute the task-performance subtree. It will check whether the battery is full. If the battery is not full, it will execute the recharge subtree.

Next, the drop-tool subtree will execute its reactive sequence. It will check whether the tool needs to be dropped. It will execute the station approach fallback and then drop the tool. While a later sequence is running, it will re-evaluate earlier sequences and stop the running sequence if an earlier task becomes applicable. It will check whether the task is monitoring and execute the monitoring subtree when true. It will check whether the task is inspection and execute the inspection subtree when true.         <SequenceStar name="RecoveryActions">
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>

Next, the pipeline sequence will execute the rate-controlled path computation and path following in order. It will stop if either action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action.

Next, the rate controller will execute the path-computation recovery node at a rate of 1 Hz.

Next, the path-computation recovery node will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose. If that action fails, it will execute the custom action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context and retry the ROS action ComputePathToPose once.

Next, the ROS action ComputePathToPose will compute a path to the goal and store the path for later use.

Next, the path-following recovery node will execute the ROS action FollowPath. If that action fails, it will execute the custom action ClearLocalCostmap-Context and retry the ROS action FollowPath once.

Next, the ROS action FollowPath will follow the stored path toward the goal.

Next, the sequence with memory will execute the local costmap clearing, global costmap clearing, spinning, and waiting actions in sequence. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart the sequence from the failed action.

First, the root NavigateRecovery recovery node will execute the main navigation subtree. If the main subtree fails, it will execute the recovery subtree and retry navigation until six recovery attempts are exhausted. If recovery fails after the retries, it will stop execution.

Next, the NavigateWithReplanning pipeline sequence will execute the RateController and FollowPath recovery node in order. It will stop if either action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will advance to the next action.

Next, the RateController will run the ComputePathToPose recovery node at a rate of 1 Hz. The ComputePathToPose recovery node will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose. If path computation fails, it will execute the ClearGlobalCostmap-Context recovery action and retry path computation once. If the recovery action fails, it will stop execution.

Next, the FollowPath recovery node will execute the ROS action FollowPath using the computed path. If path following fails, it will execute the ClearLocalCostmap-Context recovery action and retry path following once. If the recovery action fails, it will stop execution.

Finally, the RecoveryFallback reactive fallback will execute GoalUpdated and RecoveryActions in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. If GoalUpdated fails, it will execute RecoveryActions and re-evaluate GoalUpdated whenever a later action is running. If GoalUpdated then succeeds, it will halt the running recovery action and stop the fallback.

Next, the RecoveryActions sequence will execute the ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree, ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree, Spin, and Wait actions in order. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart the sequence from the failed action.

<root main_tree_to_execute="BehaviorTree">
    <!-- ////////// -->
    <BehaviorTree ID="BehaviorTree">
        <ReactiveSequence>
           <Condition ID="ConditionExample" name="CustomConditionExample"/>
           <Action ID="ActionExample" name="CustomActionExample"/>
        </ReactiveSequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a reactive task that checks a condition before executing a custom action.

First, it will execute the following actions (CustomConditionExample, CustomActionExample) in sequence. If CustomActionExample fails, it will stop execution. While CustomActionExample is still running, it will re-evaluate CustomConditionExample. If CustomConditionExample now fails, it will halt CustomActionExample and stop the sequence.

It will check whether ConditionExample is true.

It will execute custom action ActionExample after ConditionExample succeeds.

Parameters: CustomConditionExample has no ports. ActionExample has no ports.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree replans the global path periodically at 1 Hz.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <PipelineSequence name="NavigateWithReplanning">
      <SpeedController min_rate="0.1" max_rate="1.0" min_speed="0.0" max_speed="0.26" filter_duration="0.3">
        <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
      </SpeedController>
      <FollowPath path="{path}"  controller_id="FollowPath"/>
    </PipelineSequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a navigation task that periodically replans a global path and follows the current path to a goal.

First, the root PipelineSequence named NavigateWithReplanning will execute SpeedController and FollowPath in order and will stop if any action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action.

Next, the SpeedController will regulate the execution rate of ComputePathToPose between 0.1 and 1.0 Hz according to the speed range from 0.0 to 0.26 and a filter duration of 0.3 seconds. The robot will run the ROS action ComputePathToPose with the goal read from {goal}. It will store the computed path under {path}. The path computation will use the GridBased planner.

Finally, it will run the ROS action FollowPath with the path read from {path}. It will use the FollowPath controller.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will use goal={goal}, path={path}, and planner_id=GridBased. The ROS action FollowPath will use path={path} and controller_id=FollowPath. The SpeedController will use min_rate=0.1, max_rate=1.0, min_speed=0.0, max_speed=0.26, and filter_duration=0.3.

mrq:
The mission describes an escort task that repeatedly conducts a dialog and social navigation behavior.

First, the root Sequence root_sequence will execute Repeat in order and stop if Repeat fails.

Next, Repeat will execute Parallel 100 times.

Then, Parallel will execute Dialog and SocialNav2Action simultaneously. The execution will succeed when one action succeeds. The execution will fail if any action fails.

Finally, it will execute custom action Dialog and ROS action SocialNav2Action.

Parameters: The ROS action SocialNav2Action will use goal "escort" and agent_id "agent_1".

mrq:
The mission describes a fallback wildlife behavior that repeatedly attempts to acquire and attack a target, hunt at night when hungry, retreat during the day, or move randomly.

First, the FallbackStar will execute the following actions consecutively: the first SequenceStar, the SequenceStar named Hunt, the SequenceStar named Retreat, and RandomMove. If any action fails, it will move to the next action until an action succeeds. If no action succeeds, it will start all over again until an action succeeds.

Next, the first SequenceStar will execute GetTarget, Move, and the nested Sequence in sequence. If any action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next. If any action fails, it will start the sequence again from the failed action.

It will execute custom action GetTarget.

It will execute custom action Move.

The nested Sequence will execute TargetAdjacent and AttackTarget in order and will stop if any action fails.

It will check whether TargetAdjacent is true.

It will execute custom action AttackTarget.

Next, the SequenceStar named Hunt will execute IsNight, IsHungry, FindPrey, Move, KillPrey, and EatPrey in sequence. If any action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next. If any action fails, it will start the sequence again from the failed action.

It will check whether IsNight is true.

It will check whether IsHungry is true.

It will execute custom action FindPrey.

It will execute custom action Move.

It will execute custom action KillPrey.

It will execute custom action EatPrey.

Next, the SequenceStar named Retreat will execute IsDay, FindRetreat, Move, and the nested Sequence in sequence. If any action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next. If any action fails, it will start the sequence again from the failed action.

It will check whether IsDay is true.

It will execute custom action FindRetreat.

It will execute custom action Move.

The nested Sequence will execute IsDay and Sleep in order and will stop if any action fails.

It will check whether IsDay is true.

It will execute custom action Sleep.

Finally, it will execute custom action RandomMove.

Parameters: No action ports are specified.

mrq:
The mission describes vehicle motion control that prioritizes mission waiting, global path preparation, obstacle handling, lane changes, local path following, stopping, and driving.

First, the root fallback named Core_seq will execute its child sequences consecutively. If the first child sequence fails, it will move to the second child sequence. If an action in the second child sequence fails, the root fallback will not have another successful alternative.

Next, the first sequence will check whether the mission is waiting and then stop the vehicle. The checkMissionWait condition will be true before the stop action executes.

Next, the second sequence will execute global path preparation, motion control, and path setting in order. It will stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, the inner sequence will check whether a global path exists, initialize the vehicle, and select either lane-change processing or global follow-path generation. The checkExistPathGlobal condition will be true before initialization begins.

Next, the lane-selection fallback will first attempt global lane-change processing. If that processing fails, it will generate a global follow path.

Next, the global lane-change sequence will check whether a global lane change is required. It will then select left-lane or right-lane processing.

Next, the left-lane sequence will check whether a left lane change is selected. It will generate a left lane-change path when no generated lane-change path is available. It will keep the lane when collision checking succeeds. It will change to the left lane when the keep-lane sequence fails.

Next, the right-lane sequence will generate a right lane-change path when no generated lane-change path is available. It will keep the lane when collision checking succeeds. It will change to the right lane when the keep-lane sequence fails.

Next, the obstacle-handling fallback will first process a detected front object. If that processing fails, it will process a near-stopline case. If both cases fail, it will drive.

Next, the front-object sequence will check whether a front object exists. It will then choose global-follow behavior or lane and local-path behavior.

Next, the global-follow fallback named loc_check will accelerate when the vehicle is near a corner, near a stop line, or allowed to keep its lane. It will try these acceleration conditions in order.

Next, the lane-processing fallback named lane_check will check whether a lane change is required. It will then select left-lane or right-lane processing.

Next, the left-lane processing sequence will check whether a left lane change is possible. It will generate a left lane-change path when needed. It will keep the lane when collision checking succeeds. It will change to the left lane when keeping the lane fails.

Next, the right-lane processing sequence will generate a right lane-change path when needed. It will keep the lane when collision checking succeeds. It will change to the right lane when keeping the lane fails.

Next, the local path sequence named Local_path will create a local path when the local path is empty. It will stop, generate the local path, and set the local starting point in that case.

Next, the local-path fallback named local_check will set the local endpoint when the local path is finished. If a collision is detected, it will stop and generate a new local path. If neither condition succeeds, it will follow the local path.

Next, the near-stopline sequence will check whether the vehicle is near a stop line. It will then choose pass-through or stopping behavior.

Next, the pass-through fallback will check whether passing is allowed. When passing is allowed, it will stop if a collision is detected and then drive. When passing is not allowed, it will stop.

Next, the final drive action will execute when the preceding obstacle and stopline alternatives fail.

Finally, the outer sequence will set the path after global preparation and motion control succeed.

Parameters: No actions in this behavior tree define ports.

The mission describes reactive end-effector positioning that checks whether the end effector has reached the target and otherwise selects a movement goal based on its current position.

First, the root reactive fallback will execute root_sequence actions (goal_check, 3-goal, 2-traverse, SetMGGoal) in order. If an action succeeds, it will stop execution. If an action fails, it will continue to the next action. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate earlier actions. If an earlier action succeeds, it will halt the running action and stop the fallback.

Next, the robot will check whether the end-effector position is within the specified threshold of the target position.

Next, the first reactive sequence, 3-goal, will execute ee_y_threshold and mg_goal3 in sequence. If ee_y_threshold fails, it will stop the sequence. While mg_goal3 is running, it will re-evaluate ee_y_threshold. If ee_y_threshold then fails, it will halt mg_goal3 and stop the sequence.

Next, it will check whether the end-effector y-coordinate is below the y-threshold.

Next, it will execute custom action SetMGGoal to set movement goal 3 after the y-coordinate check succeeds.

Next, the second reactive sequence, 2-traverse, will execute ee_z_threshold and mg_goal2 in sequence. If ee_z_threshold fails, it will stop the sequence. While mg_goal2 is running, it will re-evaluate ee_z_threshold. If ee_z_threshold then fails, it will halt mg_goal2 and stop the sequence.

Next, it will check whether the end-effector z-coordinate is above the z-threshold.

Next, it will execute custom action SetMGGoal to set movement goal 2 after the z-coordinate check succeeds.

Finally, it will execute custom action SetMGGoal to set movement goal 1 if the preceding fallback actions fail.

Parameters: The custom action SetMGGoal will use {mp_3_x}, {mp_3_y}, and {mp_3_z} for movement goal 3 and will use {mg_trans_x}, {mg_trans_y}, and {mg_trans_z} for the movement transformation. The custom action SetMGGoal will use {mp_2_x}, {mp_2_y}, and {mp_2_z} for movement goal 2 and will use {mg_trans_x}, {mg_trans_y}, and {mg_trans_z} for the movement transformation. The custom action SetMGGoal will use {mp_1_x}, {mp_1_y}, and {mp_1_z} for movement goal 1 and will use {mg_trans_x}, {mg_trans_y}, and {mg_trans_z} for the movement transformation.

It will execute custom action DeliverObject. It will execute Repeat continuously until it fails or succeeds.

Next, the Repeat node in DefaultDeliver will execute ForceSuccess continuously until it fails or succeeds. ForceSuccess will execute Delay and make sure it always succeeds. Delay will execute delayed custom action DoNothing after the delay timer and resume after the delay period is exhausted.

Next, the Dock sequence named Charge will execute custom action dock in order and stop if the action fails. It will execute custom action dock.

Next, the Pick sequence will execute moveRoboterPosition, DetectObject, approachObject, DetectObject, and IfThenElse in order and stop if any action fails. It will execute custom action moveRoboterPosition. It will execute custom action DetectObject. It will execute custom action approachObject. It will execute custom action DetectObject.

Next, IfThenElse will execute the inverted validEstimatedPosition check. If the inverted check succeeds, it will execute the sequence containing approachObject and PickObject. Otherwise, it will execute PickObject. The Inverter will execute custom action validEstimatedPosition. If validEstimatedPosition succeeds, the inverter will return failure. The mission describes traversing an opening by passing through an already open door, opening a closed door before passing through it, or passing through a window if the door-based options fail.

First, the root fallback will execute the door-open sequence, the DoorClosed subtree, and PassThroughWindow consecutively. If any option fails, it will move to the next option until one succeeds. If no option succeeds, the execution will fail.

Next, the door-open sequence will execute IsDoorOpen and PassThroughDoor in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. It will check whether the door is open. If the door is open, it will pass through the door.

Then, the DoorClosed subtree will execute door_closed_sequence. The door_closed_sequence will execute the inverted IsDoorOpen check, the RetryUntilSuccesful decorator, and PassThroughDoor in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. The inverted IsDoorOpen check will execute IsDoorOpen and reverse its outcome. If IsDoorOpen succeeds, the inverted check will fail. If IsDoorOpen fails, the inverted check will succeed. The RetryUntilSuccesful decorator will keep trying to execute OpenDoor until it succeeds. It will retry OpenDoor according to its configured attempt limit of four attempts. After OpenDoor succeeds, it will pass through the door.

Finally, it will pass through the window when the door-open sequence and the DoorClosed subtree fail.

The mission describes a reactive battery-management behavior that checks battery and charging states, announces the battery status, waits, and attempts to reach and charge at a charging station when required.

First, the root ReactiveSequence will execute the ReactiveFallback, the battery-status announcement, and the five-second wait in order. If the ReactiveFallback fails, the sequence will stop. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate preceding actions and stop if a preceding action fails.

Next, the ReactiveFallback will execute the three battery-management sequences from left to right. If an action in a sequence succeeds, it will stop evaluating that fallback. If an action fails, it will move to the next sequence. While a later sequence is running, it will re-evaluate earlier sequences and stop the running sequence if an earlier sequence succeeds.

Next, the first Sequence will execute CheckBattery, the charged-or-good comparison, CheckCharging, and the undocked comparison in order. It will stop if any action fails. It will run custom action CheckBattery and store the battery state and percentage. It will verify that the battery state is less than 2. It will run custom action CheckCharging and store the charging state. It will verify that the charging state equals 0.

Next, the second Sequence will execute CheckBattery, the fully-charged comparison, and its nested Sequence in order. It will stop if any action fails. It will run custom action CheckBattery and store the battery state and percentage. It will verify that the battery state equals 0.

Next, the nested Sequence will execute CheckCharging, the charging comparison, and Charge in order. It will stop if any action fails. It will run custom action CheckCharging and store the charging state. It will verify that the charging state equals 1. It will run custom action Charge to undock by stopping charging.

Next, the third Sequence will execute CheckCharging, the not-docked comparison, and the ForceFailure subtree in order. It will stop if any action fails. It will run custom action CheckCharging and store the charging state. It will verify that the charging state is not equal to 1.

Next, the ForceFailure decorator will execute the Fallback and force its result to failure.

Next, the Fallback will execute RetryUntilSuccesful and Speak consecutively. If RetryUntilSuccesful fails, it will execute Speak. If both actions fail, the fallback will fail.

Next, RetryUntilSuccesful will keep trying to execute the ChargeST subtree until it succeeds. If a try fails, it will retry the subtree until it succeeds or reaches two attempts.

Next, the ChargeST subtree will execute its SequenceStar. The SequenceStar will execute Speak, WaitForXSeconds, and the Fallback in sequence. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and continue with the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from the failed action.

Next, Speak will announce hunger. WaitForXSeconds will wait for two seconds before returning success. The Fallback will execute its SequenceStar and proceed to its next child if that sequence fails.

Next, the inner SequenceStar will execute RetryUntilSuccesful and Parallel in sequence. If RetryUntilSuccesful succeeds, it will remember that action and continue to Parallel. If either action fails, it will restart from the failed action.

Next, RetryUntilSuccesful will keep trying to execute MoveBase until it succeeds. MoveBase will attempt to reach the specified first point from the map frame.

Next, Parallel will execute Charge and Repeat simultaneously. It will succeed when two actions succeed. It will fail if one action fails.
