mrq:
The mission describes battery management followed by random patrol movement, with fallback recovery through costmap clearing.

The root fallback will execute the first sequence and use the ROS action CallEmptySrv if that sequence fails.

First, the sequence will execute charging_full_st, DebugAction, GeneralActionlib, MoveBase, DebugAction, and WaitForXSeconds in order. It will stop if any action fails.

Next, charging_full_st will execute its first sequence, second sequence, third sequence, or fourth sequence consecutively. If any sequence fails, it will move to the next sequence until one succeeds. If no sequence succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, the first charging sequence will execute DebugAction, CheckBattery, CompareInt, CheckCharging, CompareInt, and ChargeST in order. It will stop if any action or condition fails. CheckBattery will store the battery state under {k_bat_state}. CompareInt will succeed when {k_bat_state} equals 3. CheckCharging will store the charging state under {charge_state}. CompareInt will succeed when {charge_state} equals 0. ChargeST will then execute its charging routine.

Next, the second charging sequence will execute DebugAction, CheckCharging, CompareInt, CheckBattery, CompareInt, Speak, and Charge in order. It will stop if any action or condition fails. CompareInt will succeed when {charge_state} equals 1. CompareInt will then succeed when {k_bat_state} equals 0. Speak will announce that the batteries are full. Charge will stop charging.

Next, the third charging sequence will execute DebugAction, CheckBattery, CompareInt, CheckCharging, CompareInt, Speak, CallEmptySrv, and WaitForXSeconds in order. It will stop if any action or condition fails. CompareInt will succeed when {k_bat_state} equals 3. CompareInt will then succeed when {charge_state} equals 0. Speak will request assistance with charging. CallEmptySrv will clear the move-base costmaps. WaitForXSeconds will wait ten seconds and return success.

Next, the fourth charging sequence will execute CheckBattery and CompareInt in order. It will stop if either action fails. CompareInt will succeed when {k_bat_state} does not equal 3.

Next, the second sequence inside charging_full_st will execute CheckCharging, CompareInt, and DebugAction in order. It will stop if any action or condition fails. CompareInt will succeed when {charge_state} equals 0. DebugAction will report that movement is possible.

Next, ChargeST will execute Speak, WaitForXSeconds, RetryUntilSuccesful, and Parallel in sequence. If any action fails, it will restart from the failed action. Speak will announce hunger. WaitForXSeconds will wait two seconds. RetryUntilSuccesful will keep trying MoveBase until it succeeds. Parallel will execute Charge and Repeat simultaneously. The parallel execution will succeed when two actions succeed and will fail when one action fails. Repeat will execute Speak ten times.

Next, the outer patrol sequence will execute DebugAction, GeneralActionlib, MoveBase, DebugAction, and WaitForXSeconds after charging_full_st succeeds. GeneralActionlib will request random movement and store its result under {result}. MoveBase will move to the stored result in the map frame. DebugAction will report arrival. WaitForXSeconds will wait five seconds.

Finally, the fallback will execute CallEmptySrv if the patrol sequence fails. CallEmptySrv will clear the service named /move_base/clear_costmaps.

Parameters: DebugAction will receive string="Vou patrulhar". GeneralActionlib will receive action_name="random_movement", constants="0,1,3", and variables="", and will store its result under {result}. MoveBase will receive goal_pose={result}, action_name="move_base", and frame_id="map". WaitForXSeconds will receive seconds="5" and result="SUCCESS". Speak will receive language="pt_PT", voice="pt-PT-Wavenet-D", utterance="Tenho fome", and action_name="/gcloud_tts". WaitForXSeconds will receive seconds="2", result="SUCCESS", and name="Wait2Seconds". MoveBase will receive goal_pose="-4.88723403052;-6.0285904746;0.0;0.0;0.0;0.997843662386;0.0503172395835", name="Go to first point", action_name="move_base", and frame_id="map". Charge will receive action_name="charging_action" and action="CHARGE". Speak will receive language="pt_PT", voice="pt-PT-Wavenet-D", utterance="bip bip", and action_name="/gcloud_tts". DebugAction will receive string="checking battery state". CheckBattery will receive percentage="k_bat_perc", service_name="/vizzy_batteries_state", and will store battery_state under {k_bat_state}. CompareInt will receive A={k_bat_state}, Condition="==", and B="3". CheckCharging will receive service_name="battery_charging_state" and will store charging_state under {charge_state}. CompareInt will receive A={charge_state}, Condition="==", and B="0". DebugAction will receive string="checking if batteries are charged". CheckBattery will receive percentage="k_bat_perc", service_name="/vizzy_batteries_state", and will store battery_state under {k_bat_state}.           <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>

mrq:
The mission describes a navigation task that repeatedly computes and follows a path while applying recovery actions when navigation fails.

First, the root PipelineSequence will execute NavigationSequence and ClearEntireCostmap-Finish in order and stop if an action fails. It will advance to the next action while the current action is running or has succeeded.

Next, the robot will execute NavigateRecovery. It will execute NavigateWithReplanning as the main action. If the main action fails, it will execute RecoveryFallback, retry NavigateWithReplanning after recovery, and stop when recovery retries are exhausted.

Next, it will execute NavigateWithReplanning in order and stop if an action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will advance to the next action.

Next, it will execute the RateController at 1.0 hertz. The RateController will execute ComputePathToPose and limit its execution rate.

Next, it will execute the RecoveryNode named ComputePathToPose. It will execute ComputePathToPose as the main action. If it fails, it will execute GlobalPlannerRecoveryActions as the recovery action. After recovery, it will retry ComputePathToPose. If recovery fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose with the goal read from {goal}. It will store the computed path under {path}. It will use the GridBased planner.

Next, it will execute GlobalPlannerRecoveryActions according to its round-robin policy. It will clear the global costmap and then wait for two seconds across successive recovery attempts.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearGlobalCostmap-Context. It will use the global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap service.

Next, it will execute the ROS action Wait for two seconds.

Next, it will execute the RecoveryNode named FollowPath. It will execute FollowPath as the main action. If it fails, it will execute ClearLocalCostmap-Context as the recovery action. After recovery, it will retry FollowPath. If recovery fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath with the path read from {path}. It will use the FollowPath controller.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearLocalCostmap-Context. It will use the local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap service.

Next, it will execute RecoveryFallback consecutively. If GoalUpdated fails, it will execute RecoveryActions. If RecoveryActions succeeds, it will stop the fallback. If no recovery action succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, it will check GoalUpdated. If the goal has been updated, this action will succeed.

Next, it will execute RecoveryActions in sequence and remember actions that have succeeded. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree. It will use the local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap service.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree. It will use the global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap service.

Next, it will execute the ROS action Spin with a spin distance of 1.57.

Next, it will execute the ROS action Wait for five seconds.

Finally, it will execute the ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearGlobalCostmap-Finish. It will use the global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap service.

Parameters: ComputePathToPose will use goal={goal}, path={path}, and planner_id=GridBased. ClearGlobalCostmap-Context will use service_name=global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap. Wait will use wait_duration=2.0. FollowPath will use path={path} and controller_id=FollowPath. ClearLocalCostmap-Context will use service_name=local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap. ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name=local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap. ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name=global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap. The mission describes a reactive safety-monitoring task that checks stop status, diagnostics, battery level, patient condition, and then runs a selected behavior.

First, the robot will execute the following actions (CheckStop, CheckDiagnosticStatus, the first Fallback, the second Fallback, and the inner Sequence) in sequence. If any action fails, the reactive sequence will stop. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate the preceding actions. If a preceding action fails, it will halt the running action and stop the sequence.

Next, it will execute CheckStop. If CheckStop fails, the reactive sequence will stop.

Next, it will execute CheckDiagnosticStatus. If CheckDiagnosticStatus fails, the reactive sequence will stop.

Next, it will execute the first Fallback consecutively. If CheckBattery fails, it will execute Recharge. If no action succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, it will execute the second Fallback consecutively. If CheckPatientCondition fails, it will execute Emergency. If no action succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Finally, it will execute the inner Sequence in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. It will run ROS action StringParameterRequest to select a behavior and store the selected value. It will execute BehaviorSwitch by comparing the selected blackboard value with the listed behavior cases. If a case matches, it will execute the corresponding behavior. If no case matches, it will execute AlwaysFailureNode and fail.

Parameters: StringParameterRequest will use title="Select a behavior", options="DevicePairingWithRequest,BaseMovementWithRequest,ArmMovementWithRequest,BatteryChargingWithRequest,FreeWalking,GuidedWalking,TransportWithDevice", and value="{selected_behavior}". BehaviorSwitch will use variable="{selected_behavior}", case_1="DevicePairingWithRequest", case_2="BaseMovementWithRequest", case_3="ArmMovementWithRequest", case_4="BatteryChargingWithRequest", case_5="FreeWalking", case_6="GuidedWalking", and case_7="TransportWithDevice".

The mission describes dynamic navigation toward an updated goal while periodically recomputing and truncating the path.

First, the root PipelineSequence named NavigateWithReplanning will execute the RateController and the KeepRunningUntilFailure in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will go to the next action.

Next, the RateController will execute the Sequence at a rate of 1.0 hertz.

Then, the Sequence will execute the GoalUpdater and the TruncatePath in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, the GoalUpdater will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose with the updated goal and store the resulting path. The GoalUpdater will provide the input goal to the ROS action ComputePathToPose and store the updated goal.

Then, the TruncatePath action will shorten the stored path to a distance of 1.0.

Finally, the KeepRunningUntilFailure will execute the ROS action FollowPath. If the ROS action FollowPath succeeds, it will restart it. If the ROS action FollowPath fails, it will stop looping and continue execution.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will use goal {updated_goal}, path {path}, and planner_id GridBased. The GoalUpdater action will use input_goal {goal} and output_goal {updated_goal}. The TruncatePath action will use distance 1.0, input_path {path}, and output_path {truncated_path}. The ROS action FollowPath will use path {truncated_path} and controller_id FollowPath.

First, it will execute the following actions (RFConditionExample, RFActionExample) in sequence. If RFConditionExample fails, it will stop execution. While RFActionExample is still running, it will re-evaluate RFConditionExample. If RFConditionExample then fails, it will halt RFActionExample and stop the sequence.

It will check RFConditionExample and continue to RFActionExample only when the condition succeeds. It will execute custom action RFActionExample after the condition succeeds.

Parameters: No action ports are defined.

mrq:
The mission describes a pick-and-place task that will return the robot home, place a held object, pick an observed object, or find a target according to the first successful fallback branch.

First, the root fallback named Pick_hold_place will execute the following actions consecutively (the Sequence named Back home, the Sequence named Place, the Sequence named Pick, and the fourth Sequence). If any action fails, it will move to the next action until an action succeeds. If no action succeeds, the execution will fail.

Next, the Sequence named Back home will execute the following actions (BTIsObjContainer, SetBlackboard, SetBlackboard, the Execution subtree, SetBlackboard, SetBlackboard, and SetBlackboard) in order and will stop the sequence if any action fails. It will check whether {tagisobjcon} indicates that the object is a container. It will set {target} to name;home. It will set {gripperout} to open. It will execute the Execution subtree with {target} and {gripperout}. It will set {tagishold} to 0. It will set {tagisobjcon} to 0. It will set {tagisobjpose} to 0.

Next, the Sequence named Place will execute the following actions (BTIsHoldObj and the Parallel node) in order and will stop the sequence if any action fails. It will check whether {tagishold} indicates that the robot holds an object. The Parallel node will execute SetBlackboard, the Execution subtree, and the Place_subtree simultaneously. The Parallel node will succeed when three actions succeed. It will set {containerpose} to pose;-0.3;0.4;0.010;0;1;0;0.0002. It will execute the Execution subtree with {target} and {gripperout}. It will execute the Place_subtree with {containerpose}, {gripperout}, {tagisobjcon}, and {target}.

Next, the Sequence named Pick will execute the following actions (BTIsObjPose and the Parallel node) in order and will stop the sequence if any action fails. It will check whether {tagisobjpose} indicates that an object pose is available. The Parallel node will execute the Execution subtree and the Pick_subtree simultaneously. The Parallel node will succeed when two actions succeed. It will execute the Execution subtree with {target} and {gripperout}. It will execute the Pick_subtree with {observedpose}, {tagishold}, {target}, and {gripperout}.

Next, the fourth Sequence will execute the following actions (BTCameraFindTarget, SetBlackboard, and SetBlackboard) in order and will stop the sequence if any action fails. It will find a target and store the object-pose result in {tagisobjpose} and the observed pose in {observedpose}. It will set {tagishold} to 0. It will set {tagisobjcon} to 0.

Next, the Execution subtree will execute its two child sequences in order while remembering successful children. If a child fails, it will restart from that failed child. The first child sequence will execute BTWaitForTarget, BTPathPlanning, and BTFollowPath in order and will stop if any action fails. It will wait for {Target} and store the resulting target in {target}. It will plan a path to {Target} and store the plan in {plan}. It will follow {plan}. The second child sequence will execute BTCheckGripperCommand and BTGripperMoveSchunk in order and will stop if any action fails. It will convert {GripperOut} into {grippercom}. It will move the gripper using {grippercom}.

Next, the Pick_subtree fallback named pick_fallback will execute its child sequences consecutively. If any child sequence fails, it will move to the next child sequence until one succeeds. If all child sequences fail, the execution will fail. The Sequence named hold will execute its two child sequences in order and will stop if any action fails. The inner sequence named went up? will set {height} to 0.03 and check that height against {ObsObjPose}. It will set {tagishold} to 1. The Sequence named go up will execute its inner sequence, set {height} to 0.03, approach {ObsObjPose} at that height, set {gripperin} to no, and advertise the no gripper command into {GripperOut}. The inner sequence named Went down to pick? will set {height} to 0 and check that height against {ObsObjPose}. The Sequence named go_down_close will execute its inner sequence, set {height} to 0, approach {ObsObjPose}, set {gripperin} to close, and advertise the close gripper command into {GripperOut}. The inner sequence named Went above obj? will set {height} to 0.05 and check that height against {ObsObjPose}. The Sequence named go_above will set {height} to 0.05, approach {ObsObjPose}, set {gripperin} to no, and advertise the no gripper command into {GripperOut}.

Next, the Place_subtree fallback will execute its child sequences consecutively. If any child sequence fails, it will move to the next child sequence until one succeeds. If all child sequences fail, the execution will fail. The Sequence named Check back will execute its inner sequence in order and will stop if any action fails. The inner sequence named Placed? will set {height} to 0.03, check that height against {ContainerPose}, and set {tagisobjcon} to 1. The Sequence named Go up will execute its inner sequence, set {height} to 0.03, approach {ContainerPose}, set {gripperin} to no, and advertise the no gripper command into {GripperOut}. The inner sequence will set {height} to -0.00 and check that height against {ContainerPose}. The Sequence named Go down into container will execute its inner sequence, set {height} to -0.0, approach {ContainerPose}, set {gripperin} to open, and advertise the open gripper command into {GripperOut}. The inner sequence will set {height} to 0.05 and check that height against {ContainerPose}. The Sequence named Go above container will set {height} to 0.05, approach {ContainerPose}, set {gripperin} to no, and advertise the no gripper command into {GripperOut}.

Parameters: BTIsObjContainer will read tagisobjconin={tagisobjcon}. BTIsHoldObj will read tagisholdin={tagishold}. BTIsObjPose will read tagisobjposein={tagisobjpose} and targetin={observedpose}, and will store its target result in {observedpose}. BTCameraFindTarget will store its pose-status result in {tagisobjpose} and its target result in {observedpose}. BTWaitForTarget will read targetin={Target} and store targetout={target}. BTPathPlanning will read goal={Target} and store makeplan={plan}. BTFollowPath will read planedplan={plan}. BTCheckGripperCommand will read commandin={GripperOut} and store commandout={grippercom}. BTGripperMoveSchunk will read commandin={grippercom}. BTCheckCondition will read heightin={height} and targetin={ObsObjPose}. BTCloseToTarget in Pick_subtree will read height={height}, targetin={ObsObjPose}, targettype=waypoint, and store targetout={Target}. BTAdvertiseGripperCommand in Pick_subtree will read commandin={gripperin} and store commandout={GripperOut}. BTCloseToTarget in Place_subtree will read height={height}, targetin={ContainerPose}, targettype=waypoint, and store targetout={Target}. BTAdvertiseGripperCommand in Place_subtree will read commandin={gripperin} and store commandout={GripperOut}.

The mission describes a target-engagement task that attempts to acquire a target, move toward it, and attack it, with random movement as a fallback.

First, the root fallback will execute the following actions consecutively (the sequence Main, RandomMove). If the sequence Main fails, it will move to RandomMove. If no action succeeds, the execution will fail.

Next, the sequence Main will execute the following actions (GetTarget, Move, the sequence at position three) in sequence. If any action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next. If any action fails, it will restart the sequence from the failed action.

Next, it will run custom action GetTarget.

Next, it will run custom action Move after GetTarget succeeds.

Next, the inner sequence will execute the following actions (TargetAdjacent, AttackTarget) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. It will check whether TargetAdjacent is true. It will run custom action AttackTarget if TargetAdjacent is true.

Finally, it will run custom action RandomMove if the sequence Main fails.

Parameters: No actions in this behavior tree have ports.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first computes a path using the global planner (ComputePathToPose).
  Then, it runs two sub-branches in parallel. The first sub-branch is a FollowPath
  operation (the local planner). In parallel, there is a rate controlled execution of
  FollowPath (the global planner). Each time a new path is computed, the path update
  is sent to the local planner. The right branch, which is the rate controlled
  ComputePathToPose, always returns RUNNING. Because the Parallel node uses a
  threshold of 1, whenever the FollowPath returns SUCCESS or FAILURE, the parallel
  node will return this result.

  The goal (input to the global planner) and the resulting path (output of the global
  planner and input to the local planner) are passed on the blackboard.

  The rate at which the ComputePathToPose operation is invoked can be controlled with
  the hz parameter to the RateController node.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <RateController hz="1.0">
        <Fallback>
          <GoalReached/>
          <ComputePathToPose goal="${goal}"/>
        </Fallback>
      </RateController>
      <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a navigation task that periodically computes a path toward a goal and then follows the resulting path.

First, the root Sequence named root will execute the RateController subtree followed by FollowPath in order and will stop if either action fails.

Next, the RateController will control the execution rate at 1.0 hertz. It will execute its Fallback child consecutively. If GoalReached fails, it will execute ComputePathToPose. If no child succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Finally, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath using the path stored under {path} after the rate-controlled subtree succeeds.

Parameters: RateController will use hz="1.0". ComputePathToPose will use goal="${goal}". FollowPath will use path="${path}".

<!--
  This Behavior Tree follows a dynamic pose to a certain distance
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="20" name="NavigateRecovery">
      <PipelineSequence name="NavigateWithReplanning">
        <RateController hz="1.0">
          <Sequence>
            <GoalUpdater input_goal="{goal}" output_goal="{updated_goal}">
              <ComputePathToPose goal="{updated_goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
            </GoalUpdater>
          </Sequence>
        </RateController>
        <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
          <FollowPath path="{path}" controller_id="FollowPath"/>
        </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
      </PipelineSequence>
      <ReactiveFallback name="RecoveryFallback">
        <GoalUpdated/>
        <RoundRobin name="RecoveryActions">
          <Sequence name="ClearingActions">
            <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
            <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
            <ComputePathToPose goal="{updated_goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
          </Sequence>
          <Wait wait_duration="0.2"/>
        </RoundRobin>
      </ReactiveFallback>
    </RecoveryNode>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

mrq:
The mission describes dynamic navigation toward an updated pose with continuous path following and recovery actions.

First, the RecoveryNode NavigateRecovery will execute the main navigation subtree. If the main subtree fails, it will execute the recovery subtree and retry the main subtree until 20 recovery attempts are exhausted.

Next, the PipelineSequence NavigateWithReplanning will execute RateController and KeepRunningUntilFailure in order and stop if any action fails. While RateController is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to KeepRunningUntilFailure.

Next, the RateController will regulate execution at 1.0 Hz. It will execute its child sequence at that rate.

Next, the inner Sequence will execute GoalUpdater in order and stop if it fails. The GoalUpdater will update the goal and execute its child using the updated goal.

Next, the ROS action ComputePathToPose will compute a path to the updated goal. It will store the computed path for later use.

Next, the KeepRunningUntilFailure will execute the ROS action FollowPath. If FollowPath succeeds, it will restart it. If FollowPath fails, it will stop looping and continue execution.

The mission describes operating a coffee machine by opening it, cleaning it, placing a coffee cup, selecting the desired coffee, and completing the drink preparation.

First, the root sequence will execute the following actions (OpenCoffeeMachine, AutoClean, PutCoffeeCup, CoffeeType) in order and stop if any action fails.

Next, the OpenCoffeeMachine fallback will first check whether the machine is open. If the machine is not open, it will execute the sequence that prepares a clean cup and switches on the machine. The sequence will retry the IsCleanCupReady condition up to 10 attempts. It will then check whether the machine is open for up to 60 seconds. If the machine is still not open, it will switch on the coffee machine.

Next, the AutoClean fallback will first check whether the cleaning process is finished. If the cleaning process is not finished, it will execute the water-management fallback. If the water-management fallback fails, it will execute the waste-management fallback.

Next, the water-management fallback will first check whether there is enough water. If there is not enough water, it will execute the water-preparation sequence. The water-preparation sequence will wait up to 120 seconds for the water tank to be removed. It will then check whether the water tank is full for up to 120 seconds. If the tank is not full, it will fill the water tank. It will then wait up to 120 seconds for the water tank to be placed in the coffee machine. It will finally wait up to 120 seconds for the cleaning process to finish.

Next, the waste-management fallback will invert the IsMarroTankFull condition. If the marro tank is not full, this branch will succeed. If the marro tank is full, it will execute the waste-management sequence. The waste-management sequence will wait up to 120 seconds for the marro tank to be removed. It will then check whether the marro tank is empty for up to 120 seconds. If the tank is not empty, it will empty the marro tank. It will retry the IsMarroTankPlacedInCoffeeMachine condition up to 15 attempts. It will finally wait up to 120 seconds for the cleaning process to finish.

Next, the PutCoffeeCup fallback will check whether the coffee cup is ready for up to 120 seconds. If the coffee cup is not ready, it will place the coffee cup.

Next, the CoffeeType sequence will execute the following actions (the coffee-selection fallback, the coffee-finished check, the cup-removal check, the cleaning-cup fallback, the milk fallback, and the sugar fallback) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. The coffee-selection fallback will check whether the desired coffee is selected for up to 120 seconds. If the desired coffee is not selected, it will press the desired coffee button. It will then wait up to 120 seconds for the coffee to finish. It will wait up to 120 seconds for the cup of coffee to be removed. It will then wait up to 120 seconds for a cleaning cup to be added or for the cleaning-cup sequence to succeed. The cleaning-cup sequence will place a clean cup and switch off the coffee machine.

Next, the milk fallback will wait up to 600 seconds for a human to add milk. If milk is not added, it will check the inverted IsMilkDesired condition. If milk is desired, the inverted condition will fail and it will add milk to the coffee. The milk fallback will execute within a 120-second timeout.

Finally, the sugar fallback will wait up to 600 seconds for a human to add sugar. If sugar is not added, it will check the inverted IsSugarDesired condition. If sugar is desired, the inverted condition will fail and it will add sugar to the coffee. The sugar fallback will execute within a 120-second timeout.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first computes a path using the global planner (ComputePathToPose).
  Then, it runs two sub-branches in parallel. The first sub-branch is a FollowPath
  operation (the local planner). In parallel, there is a rate controlled execution of
  FollowPath (the global planner). Each time a new path is computed, the path update
  is sent to the local planner. The right branch, which is the rate controlled
  ComputePathToPose, always returns RUNNING. Because the Parallel node uses a
  threshold of 1, whenever the FollowPath returns SUCCESS or FAILURE, the parallel
  node will return this result.

  The goal (input to the global planner) and the resulting path (output of the global
  planner and input to the local planner) are passed on the blackboard.

  The rate at which the ComputePathToPose operation is invoked can be controlled with
  the hz parameter to the RateController node.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <RateController hz="1.0">
        <Fallback>
          <GoalReached/>
          <ComputePathToPose goal="${goal}"/>
        </Fallback>
      </RateController>
      <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Then, the fallback will execute GoalReached and ComputePathToPose consecutively. If GoalReached fails, it will execute ComputePathToPose. If neither action succeeds, the fallback execution will fail.

Finally, it will execute FollowPath after the rate-controlled fallback succeeds.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will use goal ${goal}. The ROS action FollowPath will use path ${path}. The RateController will use a rate of 1.0 hertz.

The mission describes configuring navigation parameters, computing an initial path, repeatedly replanning the path, following the path, and performing recovery actions after navigation failures.

First, the root RestoreConfig node for /footprint_publisher will execute its child and restore the configuration for /footprint_publisher.

Next, the nested RestoreConfig node for /controller_server will execute its child and restore the configuration for /controller_server.

Next, the nested RestoreConfig node for /global_costmap/global_costmap will execute its child and restore the configuration for /global_costmap/global_costmap.

Next, the Sequence node will execute ChangeParamFootprintToSmall, ChangeParamSpeedDown, ChangeParamFollowPathXyGoalTolerance, ChangeParamFollowPathYawGoalTolerance, ChangeParamWalkWeightToCenter, ChangeParamToAdjust, ChangeParamPathAdjustedCenter, ChangeParamInflationRadius, InitialComputePathRepeat, and NavigateRecovery in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, the RecoveryNode InitialComputePathRepeat will execute the main ComputePathSequence action. If it fails, it will execute the recovery action and retry the main action. If the recovery action fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, the ComputePathSequence sequence will execute ClearGlobalCostmap-context, WaitFloat, ComputePathToPose, and CheckPath in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ClearGlobalCostmap-context to clear the global costmap.

Next, it will wait for 0.5 seconds.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose to compute a path to the goal.

Next, it will execute the custom action CheckPath to check the temporary path and store the resulting path.

Next, the ForceSuccess node will execute WaitFloat and make sure it always succeeds.

Next, it will wait for 0.5 seconds.

mrq:
The mission describes a sequential behavior that evaluates failure handling, performs a blackboard check, executes a forced blackboard update, and then runs the Pippo action.

First, the root sequence will execute the following actions in order: the fallback, the DoSequenceStar sequence, the inverter, and the reactive sequence. It will stop if any action fails.

Next, the fallback will execute its reactive fallback child consecutively. If the reactive fallback fails, it will move to the next child, but no next child exists, so the fallback will fail.

Then, the reactive fallback will execute its repeat child. If that child succeeds, execution will stop. If it fails, it will continue evaluating available children, but no additional child exists.

Next, the repeat node will execute the AlwaysFailure action one time. The AlwaysFailure action will fail, so the repeat node will fail.

Then, the DoSequenceStar sequence will execute its retry-until-successful child in order. If the child succeeds, the sequence will remember the success and continue. If the child fails, the sequence will restart from the failed child.

Next, the retry-until-successful node will keep trying to execute the blackboard check until it succeeds. The blackboard check will find the value at the empty key and check whether it matches the empty expected value.

Then, the inverter will execute its ForceFailure child with the result inverted. The ForceFailure node will execute its ForceSuccess child and make sure it always fails. The ForceSuccess node will execute the SetBlackboard action and make sure it always succeeds. The SetBlackboard action will store the value “value” under the empty output key. The inverter will reverse the forced failure and return success.

Finally, the reactive sequence will execute the Pippo action in sequence. If Pippo fails, the reactive sequence will stop.

Parameters: The Repeat action will use num_cycles="1". The SetBlackboard action will use value="value" and output_key="".

The mission describes a vehicle-control behavior that waits when required, initializes global-path operation, selects lane keeping, lane changing, or A* navigation, publishes data, and provides a fallback global-following routine.

First, the root fallback named Core_seq will execute its child sequences consecutively. If any child sequence fails, it will move to the next child sequence until one succeeds. If no child sequence succeeds, the execution will fail.

Next, the first sequence will execute the checkMissionWait condition and the stop action in order. If checkMissionWait is true, it will move to stop. If checkMissionWait is false, the sequence will end.

Next, the Init sequence will execute checkExistPathGlobal, init, StateSelect, and publishData in order. If any action fails, the sequence will stop.

Next, the StateSelect fallback will execute LaneKeeping, LaneChangeLeft, LaneChangeRigth, Astar, and Recovery consecutively. If any child succeeds, it will stop. If all preceding children fail, Recovery will execute and fail.

Next, the LaneKeeping sequence will execute checkStateLaneKeeping, genPathLaneKeeping, setPath, and its inner fallback in order. If any action fails, the sequence will stop.

Next, the inner lane-keeping fallback will execute its front-object sequence, its global-lane-change sequence, and setStateLaneKeeping consecutively. If any child succeeds, it will stop. If all preceding children fail, it will execute setStateLaneKeeping.

Next, the front-object sequence will execute checkFrontObject and its decision fallback in order. If checkFrontObject is true, it will evaluate the decision fallback. If checkFrontObject is false, the sequence will end.

Next, the decision fallback will first execute the local acceleration fallback. If that fallback fails, it will execute state_change.

Next, the local acceleration fallback will execute the near-corner sequence, the near-stopline sequence, and the profit-keeping-lane sequence consecutively. If any condition is true, it will execute acc and stop evaluating alternatives. If all conditions are false, it will execute state_change.

Next, each acceleration sequence will check its corresponding condition and execute acc when that condition is true. The conditions are checkNearCorner, checkNearStopline, and checkProfitKeeplane.

Next, the state_change fallback will execute lane_change_left, lane_change_right, and astar consecutively. If a maneuver succeeds, it will stop. If all maneuvers fail, the fallback will fail.

Next, the lane_change_left sequence will execute checkLaneChangeableLeft, genPathLaneChangeLeft, and its maneuver fallback in order. If checkLaneChangeableLeft is true, it will generate the left lane-change path and evaluate the maneuver fallback.

Next, the left maneuver fallback will first execute the collision sequence. If that sequence fails, it will execute the left lane-change sequence.

Next, the left collision sequence will execute checkCollision, setStateLaneKeeping, and keepLane in order. If checkCollision is true, it will set the lane-keeping state and keep the lane.

Next, the left lane-change sequence will execute setStateLaneChangeLeft and laneChangeLeft in order. It will set the left lane-change state before changing lanes.

Next, the lane_change_right sequence will execute checkLaneChangeableRight, genPathLaneChangeRight, and its maneuver fallback in order. If checkLaneChangeableRight is true, it will generate the right lane-change path and evaluate the maneuver fallback.

Next, the right maneuver fallback will first execute the collision sequence. If that sequence fails, it will execute the right lane-change sequence.

Next, the right collision sequence will execute checkCollision, setStateLaneKeeping, and keepLane in order. If checkCollision is true, it will set the lane-keeping state and keep the lane.

Next, the right lane-change sequence will execute setStateLaneChangeRight and laneChangeRight in order. It will set the right lane-change state before changing lanes.

Next, the astar sequence will execute checkAbleAstar and its local-path sequence in order. If checkAbleAstar is true, it will evaluate local-path availability.

Next, the local-path sequence will execute checkEmptyLocal and Gen_Local in order. If checkEmptyLocal is true, it will execute Gen_Local.

Next, the Gen_Local sequence will execute stop, setStateAstar, and genPathAstar in order. It will stop, select the A* state, and generate an A* path.

Next, the global-lane-change sequence will execute checkGlobalLaneChange and its direction-selection fallback in order. If checkGlobalLaneChange is true, it will evaluate the direction-selection fallback.

Next, the direction-selection fallback will execute the left-change sequence first. If that sequence fails, it will execute the right-change sequence.

Next, the left-change sequence will execute checkLeftChange, its path-generation fallback, and its maneuver fallback in order. If checkLeftChange is true, it will generate a left lane-change path when necessary and select a left-lane maneuver.

Next, the left path-generation fallback will check checkGenPathLaneChange. If the check is false, it will execute genPathLaneChangeLeft.

Next, the left maneuver fallback will first execute the collision sequence. If that sequence fails, it will execute setStateLaneChangeLeft and laneChangeLeft.

Next, the right-change sequence will execute its path-generation fallback and its maneuver fallback in order. It will generate a right lane-change path when necessary and select a right-lane maneuver.

Next, the right path-generation fallback will check checkGenPathLaneChange. If the check is false, it will execute genPathLaneChangeRight.

Next, the right maneuver fallback will first execute the collision sequence. If that sequence fails, it will execute setStateLaneChangeRight and laneChangeRight.

Next, the LaneChangeLeft sequence will execute checkStateLaneChangeLeft, setPath, and its state fallback in order. If the state condition is true, it will set the path and evaluate collision and completion conditions.

Next, the left state fallback will execute the collision sequence, the completion sequence, and setStateLaneChangeLeft consecutively. If either condition succeeds, it will set the lane-keeping state. If both conditions fail, it will maintain the left lane-change state.

Next, the LaneChangeRigth sequence will execute checkStateLaneChangeRight, setPath, and its state fallback in order. If the state condition is true, it will set the path and evaluate collision and completion conditions.

Next, the right state fallback will execute the collision sequence, the completion sequence, and setStateLaneChangeRight consecutively. If either condition succeeds, it will set the lane-keeping state. If both conditions fail, it will maintain the right lane-change state.

Next, the Astar sequence will execute checkStateAstar, setPath, and local_check in order. If checkStateAstar is true, it will set the path and evaluate local navigation.

Next, the local_check fallback will execute the collision-recovery sequence, the A* completion sequence, and localPathfollow consecutively. If an earlier child succeeds, it will stop. If both earlier children fail, it will execute localPathfollow.

Next, the collision-recovery sequence will execute checkCollision, stop, and genPathAstar in order. If checkCollision is true, it will stop and generate another A* path.

Next, the A* completion sequence will execute checkFinishAstar, setFinishLocal, and setStateLaneKeeping in order. If checkFinishAstar is true, it will mark local navigation as finished and select lane keeping.

Next, the Recovery sequence will execute AlwaysFailure and fail.

Next, the final root sequence will execute AlwaysFailure, its global-path sequence, setPath, its driving fallback, and setPath in order. Because AlwaysFailure will fail, this sequence will not proceed beyond its first child.

First, the root Repeat node will execute its child sequence 1 time.

Next, the Sequence node will execute Nav2ClearLocalCostMap, Nav2ClearGlobalCostMap, SetBlackboard, and Nav2ComputePathClient in order and will stop if any action fails.

Then, it will run the custom action Nav2ClearLocalCostMap.

After that, it will run the custom action Nav2ClearGlobalCostMap.

Next, it will run the custom action SetBlackboard to store the goal value.

Finally, it will run the custom action Nav2ComputePathClient using the stored goal.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first goes into a branch where it will check if the robot is stuck.
  If that is the case, it will attempt to recover. Otherwise it will continue with
  the navigation branch. In this case the navigation branch is based on `parallel.xml`.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <FallbackStar name="check_motion">
        <Inverter name="is_not_stuck">
          <IsStuck/>
        </Inverter>
        <SequenceStar name="stuck_recovery">
          <Stop/>
          <BackUp/>
          <Spin/>
        </SequenceStar>
      </FallbackStar>
      <SequenceStar name="navigate">
        <ComputePathToPose endpoints="${endpoints}" path="${path}"/>
        <ParallelNode threshold="1">
          <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
          <Sequence>
            <RateController hz="2">
              <ComputePathToPose endpoints="${endpoints}" path="${path}"/>
            </RateController>
            <UpdatePath/>
          </Sequence>
        </ParallelNode>
      </SequenceStar>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a navigation task that checks for a stuck condition, performs recovery when necessary, computes a path, follows the path, and updates the path during navigation.

First, the root sequence will execute check_motion followed by navigate in order and will stop if either subtree fails.

Next, check_motion will execute is_not_stuck followed by stuck_recovery until one action succeeds. If an action fails, it will move to the next action. If all actions fail, it will restart from is_not_stuck.

It will execute inverted IsStuck. If IsStuck succeeds, it will reverse the result to failure. If IsStuck fails, it will reverse the result to success.

If is_not_stuck fails, it will execute stuck_recovery as a remembered sequence. It will execute Stop, BackUp, and Spin in order. After an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action.

Then, navigate will execute ComputePathToPose followed by the parallel navigation operations in sequence. After an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action.

It will compute a path with ROS action ComputePathToPose using the endpoints and store the resulting path.

It will execute the parallel navigation operations simultaneously. The parallel operation will succeed when at least one child succeeds. It will fail if any child fails.

It will execute ROS action FollowPath using the computed path.

It will execute the path-refresh sequence in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. It will run RateController at 2 Hz. It will run ROS action ComputePathToPose through RateController using the endpoints and store the refreshed path. It will then run UpdatePath.

Parameters: ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive endpoints="${endpoints}" and path="${path}". ROS action FollowPath will receive path="${path}". RateController will receive hz="2". The second ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive endpoints="${endpoints}" and path="${path}".

            <InitNode name="Init"/>

            <Fallback name="get_tool_fallback">

                    <DriveToNode name="DriveTo" goal="pick"/>
                    <MoveItNode name="MoveIt" function="CaptureObject"/>
                    <MoveItNode name="MoveIt" function="PickUpObject"/>

        </RecoveryNode>
      </PipelineSequence>
      <SequenceStar name="RecoveryActions">

mrq:
The mission describes navigation to a goal with periodic global-path replanning and recovery actions.

First, the robot will execute the main navigation action. If the main navigation action fails, it will execute the recovery actions and retry the main navigation action. If the recovery actions fail and retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, it will execute the actions in NavigateWithReplanning in order and advance to the next action while the current action is running or has succeeded. It will stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, it will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose through the rate controller at 1.0 Hz. It will retry ComputePathToPose once if it fails. If ComputePathToPose still fails, it will execute the ROS service ClearEntireCostmap for the global costmap. It will use {goal} as the goal and store the computed path under {path}. It will use the GridBased planner.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath after the preceding action is running or has succeeded. It will retry FollowPath once if it fails. If FollowPath still fails, it will execute the ROS service ClearEntireCostmap for the local costmap. It will use the path stored under {path}. It will use the FollowPath controller.

Finally, it will execute the recovery actions in sequence while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart the sequence from that failed action. It will execute the ROS service ClearEntireCostmap for the local costmap. It will execute the ROS service ClearEntireCostmap for the global costmap. It will execute the ROS action Wait after the costmaps are cleared.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will use goal={goal}, path={path}, and planner_id=GridBased. The ROS service ClearEntireCostmap in the path-recovery subtree will use service_name=global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap. The ROS action FollowPath will use path={path} and controller_id=FollowPath. The ROS service ClearEntireCostmap in the path-following subtree will use service_name=local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap. The ROS service ClearEntireCostmap in the recovery sequence will use service_name=local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap. The ROS service ClearEntireCostmap in the recovery sequence will use service_name=global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap. The ROS action Wait will use wait_duration=2.

The mission describes a trader’s recurring behavior for satisfying hunger, thirst, and sleep needs before leaving the area or working at a market stall.

First, the root fallback GnomeTrader will execute Needs and then Jobs consecutively. If an action in Needs fails, it will try Jobs. If all actions fail, it will restart from Needs until an action succeeds.

Next, the fallback Needs will execute Hunger, Thirst, and Sleepy consecutively. If one subtree fails, it will try the next subtree. If all subtrees fail, it will restart from Hunger until one subtree succeeds.

Next, the Hunger sequence Hunger will execute its actions in order while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. Its fallback will repeatedly try the sequence that checks IsHungry and finds food until that sequence succeeds. It will then move, pick up an item, and force the dining sequence to succeed. The dining sequence will find dining and move. It will then eat.

Next, the Thirst sequence Thirst will execute its actions in order while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. Its fallback will repeatedly try the sequence that checks IsThirsty and finds a drink until that sequence succeeds. It will then move, pick up an item, and force the dining sequence to succeed. The dining sequence will find dining and move. It will then drink.

Next, the Sleepy sequence Sleep will execute its actions in order while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. It will check IsSleepy. It will force the sequence that finds a bed and moves to succeed. It will then sleep.

Next, the Jobs fallback will execute Leave and WorkAtMarketStall consecutively. If an action in Leave fails, it will try WorkAtMarketStall. If all actions fail, it will restart from Leave until one action succeeds.

Next, the Leave sequence will execute its actions in order while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. It will check IsTimeToLeave. It will get the exit position, move, and leave the map.

Next, the WorkAtMarketStall sequence will execute its actions in order while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. It will get the market stall position, move, and trade.

Next, the StandardJobs sequence will execute its actions in order while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. mrq:
The mission describes a job-execution behavior that retrieves a job, selects the matching job procedure, and performs the required work or aborts when execution fails.

First, the root will execute the Jobs subtree.

Next, the Jobs sequence will execute GetJob and then repeatedly evaluate the available job procedures until one succeeds. The robot will run GetJob. It will evaluate JobButcherAnimal, JobDyeAnimal, JobLeadAnimalToPasture, JobHarvestAnimal, JobTameAnimal, JobHaulMultiple, and JobStandard in order. If a job procedure fails, it will evaluate the next procedure. If every procedure fails, it will restart evaluation from JobButcherAnimal.

Next, the JobButcherAnimal precondition will compare the blackboard value at JobType with ButcherAnimal. If the values match, its fallback will try the butchering sequence and will execute AbortJob if that sequence fails. The butchering sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ButcherAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If an action succeeds, the sequence will remember it and continue with the next action. If an action fails, the sequence will restart from that failed action.

Next, the JobDyeAnimal precondition will compare the blackboard value at JobType with DyeAnimal. If the values match, its fallback will try the dyeing sequence and will execute AbortJob if that sequence fails. The dyeing sequence will execute InitJob, ClaimItems, MoveAllItemsToJob, InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, DyeAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If an action succeeds, the sequence will remember it and continue with the next action. If an action fails, the sequence will restart from that failed action.

Next, the JobLeadAnimalToPasture precondition will compare the blackboard value at JobType with LeadAnimalToPasture. If the values match, its fallback will try the leading sequence and will execute AbortJob if that sequence fails. The leading sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If an action succeeds, the sequence will remember it and continue with the next action. If an action fails, the sequence will restart from that failed action.

Next, the JobHarvestAnimal precondition will compare the blackboard value at JobType with HarvestAnimal. If the values match, its fallback will try the harvesting sequence and will execute AbortJob if that sequence fails. The harvesting sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, HarvestAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If an action succeeds, the sequence will remember it and continue with the next action. If an action fails, the sequence will restart from that failed action.

Next, the JobTameAnimal precondition will compare the blackboard value at JobType with TameAnimal. If the values match, its fallback will try the taming sequence and will execute AbortJob if that sequence fails. The taming sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, TameAnimal, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If an action succeeds, the sequence will remember it and continue with the next action. If an action fails, the sequence will restart from that failed action.

Next, the JobHaulMultiple precondition will compare the blackboard value at JobType with HauleMultipleItems. If the values match, its fallback will try the hauling sequence and will execute AbortJob if that sequence fails. The hauling sequence will execute InitJob, FindTool, Move, EquipTool, the inverted item-pickup loop, AllPickedUp, GetItemDropPosition, Move, DropAllItems, and FinishJob in order. If an action succeeds, the sequence will remember it and continue with the next action. If an action fails, the sequence will restart from that failed action.

Next, the inverted item-pickup loop will execute its inner sequence with reversed success and failure results. The inner sequence will invert the AllPickedUp condition, execute Move and PickUpItem, and then execute ReturnAlwaysRunning. The loop will continue while the inner sequence does not succeed.

Next, the JobStandard fallback will try the standard job sequence and will execute AbortJob if that sequence fails. The standard job sequence will execute InitJob, ClaimItems, FindTool, Move, EquipTool, MoveAllItemsToJob, GetWorkPosition, Move, Work, and FinishJob in order. If an action succeeds, the sequence will remember it and continue with the next action. If an action fails, the sequence will restart from that failed action.

Parameters: The BB_Precondition for JobButcherAnimal will use key JobType and expected value ButcherAnimal. The BB_Precondition for JobDyeAnimal will use key JobType and expected value DyeAnimal. The BB_Precondition for JobLeadAnimalToPasture will use key JobType and expected value LeadAnimalToPasture. The BB_Precondition for JobHarvestAnimal will use key JobType and expected value HarvestAnimal. The BB_Precondition for JobTameAnimal will use key JobType and expected value TameAnimal. The BB_Precondition for JobHaulMultiple will use key JobType and expected value HauleMultipleItems.

mrq:
The mission describes a robot movement task that sets a movement goal, attempts to move to that goal, records the movement result, and reports the result.

First, the root sequence main_sequence will execute SetBlackboard, MoveRobot, and SaySomething in order and will stop if any action fails.

Next, the robot will execute SetBlackboard to store the value “1;2;3” under the blackboard key {move_goal}. It will execute the MoveRobot subtree with {move_goal} as the target and will store the subtree result under {move_result}. It will execute SaySomething to communicate the stored movement result.

Next, the fallback move_robot_main will execute its child actions consecutively. If an action fails, it will move to the next action until one succeeds. If no action succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, the SequenceStar will execute MoveBase and SetBlackboard in sequence. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from the failed action. It will execute MoveBase using the target stored under {target}. It will store “mission accomplished” under the blackboard key {output} after MoveBase succeeds.

Finally, ForceFailure will execute SetBlackboard and will always fail. It will store “mission failed” under the blackboard key {output}.

Parameters: SetBlackboard will use output_key="move_goal" and value="1;2;3". MoveRobot will use target="move_goal" and output="move_result". SaySomething will use message="{move_result}". MoveBase will use goal="{target}". SetBlackboard will use output_key="output" and value="mission accomplished". SetBlackboard will use output_key="output" and value="mission failed".

First, the root Repeat node will execute the enclosed Sequence {num_cycles} times.

Next, the Sequence will execute the Fallback, ReactiveSequence, and UpdateLTL in order and stop if any child fails.

Next, the Fallback will execute the LTLPreCheck condition first and will use the forced-failure ReplanningRequestLevel2 branch if LTLPreCheck fails. If both branches fail, the Fallback will fail.

Next, the LTLPreCheck condition will check ltl_state_current against ltl_state_desired_sequence and ltl_state_executed_sequence. The forced-failure branch will execute ReplanningRequestLevel2 and will force its result to fail.

Next, the ReactiveSequence will execute its four Fallback nodes in order. If a child fails, it will stop execution. While a later child is running, it will re-evaluate the preceding children and will halt the running child if a preceding child fails.

Next, the first Fallback will execute FakeDetectionLevel1. If FakeDetectionLevel1 fails, it will execute ReplanningRequestLevel1 and force that branch to fail. If both branches fail, the Fallback will fail.

Next, the second Fallback will execute the ReactiveLTLStateCheck condition. If the condition fails, it will execute ReplanningRequestLevel2 and force that branch to fail. If both branches fail, the Fallback will fail.

Next, the third Fallback will execute FakeDetectionLevel3. If FakeDetectionLevel3 fails, it will execute ReplanningRequestLevel3 and force that branch to fail. If both branches fail, the Fallback will fail.

Next, the fourth Fallback will execute the Switch6 node and then the forced-failure ReplanningRequestLevel3 branch if the switch fails. If both branches fail, the Fallback will fail.

Next, the Switch6 node will read {bt_action_type} and compare it with the cases move, stay, pick, drop, reset, and start_guiding. If the value is move, it will execute MoveAction. If the value is stay, it will execute StayAction. If the value is pick, it will execute PickAction. If the value is drop, it will execute DropActionNew. If the value is reset, it will execute ResetAction. If the value is start_guiding, it will execute GuideActionNew. If no case matches, it will execute AlwaysFailure.

Next, the UpdateLTL action will execute after the ReactiveSequence succeeds and will update the action sequence, executed action sequence, desired logical state sequence, action type, and current action.

The mission describes continuous navigation to a goal with path replanning, path following, and recovery actions for planning, control, and general system failures.

First, the root recovery node will execute the main navigation subtree. If the main navigation subtree fails, it will execute a recovery action and retry the main navigation subtree until the retry limit is exhausted.

Next, the pipeline sequence will execute the rate-controlled path-planning subtree and the path-following recovery subtree in order. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action. It will stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, the rate controller will execute the path-planning recovery subtree at a frequency of 1.0 Hz.

Next, the path-planning recovery node will execute the path-computation action. If path computation fails, it will execute the path-planning recovery fallback. After recovery, it will retry path computation. If recovery fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop the path-planning subtree.

Next, the path-planning recovery fallback will execute its actions in order. If the goal-updated check fails, it will clear the global costmap. If no recovery action succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, the robot will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose with the goal read from {goal}. It will store the computed path under {path}. It will use the GridBased planner.

Next, the path-following recovery node will execute the path-following action. If path following fails, it will execute the path-following recovery fallback. After recovery, it will retry path following. If recovery fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop the path-following subtree.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath with the path read from {path}. It will use the FollowPath controller.

Next, the path-following recovery fallback will execute its actions in order. If the goal-updated check fails, it will clear the local costmap. If no recovery action succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Finally, the general recovery fallback will execute its actions in order. If the goal-updated check succeeds, it will stop recovery. If the goal-updated check fails, it will execute the round-robin recovery actions.

Next, the round-robin recovery node will execute the clearing sequence, the spin action, the wait action, and the backup action in rotation.

Next, the clearing sequence will execute the local costmap clearing action and the global costmap clearing action in order. It will stop the sequence if either action fails.

Next, it will clear the local costmap. It will then clear the global costmap.

Next, it will rotate by 1.57 radians.

Next, it will wait for 5 seconds.

Next, it will back up 0.15 meters at a speed of 0.025 meters per second.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will use goal={goal}, path={path}, and planner_id=GridBased. The ROS action FollowPath will use path={path} and controller_id=FollowPath. The rate controller will use hz=1.0. The local costmap clearing actions will use service_name=local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap. The global costmap clearing actions will use service_name=global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap. The spin action will use spin_dist=1.57. The wait action will use wait_duration=5. The backup action will use backup_dist=0.15 and backup_speed=0.025.

        </RecoveryNode>

        <GoalUpdated/>
        <SequenceStar name="RecoveryActions">
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>

The mission describes navigating to a goal while periodically replanning the global path and performing recovery actions when navigation fails.

First, the robot will execute main NavigateWithReplanning. If it fails, it will execute recovery action RecoveryFallback. After recovery, it will retry main NavigateWithReplanning. If recovery action RecoveryFallback fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, it will execute the following actions (RateController, FollowPath) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will go to the next action.

Next, it will execute delayed ComputePathToPose after the rate timer. After the delay period is exhausted, it will resume execution.

Next, it will execute main ComputePathToPose. If it fails, it will execute recovery action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context. After recovery, it will retry main ComputePathToPose. If recovery action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, it will execute main FollowPath. If it fails, it will execute recovery action ClearLocalCostmap-Context. After recovery, it will retry main FollowPath. If recovery action ClearLocalCostmap-Context fails and retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, it will execute the following actions (GoalUpdated, SequenceStar RecoveryActions) in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will keep executing and re-evaluating previous actions whenever an action is running. If GoalUpdated then succeeds, it will halt the running action and stop the fallback.

Next, it will execute the following actions (ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree, ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree, Spin, Wait) in sequence. If any action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next. If any action fails, it will start the sequence again from the failed action.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive goal="{goal}", store its result under path="{path}", and use planner_id="GridBased". The ROS action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context will use service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap". The ROS action FollowPath will receive path="{path}" and use controller_id="FollowPath". The ROS action ClearLocalCostmap-Context will use service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap". The ROS action ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap". The ROS action ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap". The ROS action Spin will use spin_dist="1.57". The ROS action Wait will use wait_duration="5".

The mission describes a driving task that prioritizes collision avoidance, road-feature handling, lane management, and cruising.

First, the root fallback named Priorities will execute its child branches consecutively. If a branch fails, it will move to the next branch until one succeeds. If no branch succeeds, the mission will fail.

Next, the inverter will execute the Fallback named Avoid Collisions and reverse its result. If the collision-avoidance fallback succeeds, the inverter will fail. If the collision-avoidance fallback fails, the inverter will succeed.

Next, the Fallback named Avoid Collisions will execute its children consecutively. If the condition No Obstacle Ahead? fails, it will execute the fallback containing Replan Around Obstacle and Emergency Brake. If Replan Around Obstacle fails, it will execute Emergency Brake. If both actions fail, the collision-avoidance fallback will fail.

Next, the Fallback named Road Features will execute Intersection, Roundabout, and Stop consecutively. If one subtree succeeds, it will stop evaluating the remaining subtrees. If all three subtrees fail, the road-features fallback will fail.

Next, the Intersection subtree will execute its sequence in order and stop if any action fails. It will check whether Intersection Ahead is true. If the condition is true, it will approach the intersection, wait, enter the intersection, and leave the intersection in that order.

Next, the Roundabout subtree will execute its sequence in order and stop if any action fails. It will check whether Roundabout Ahead? is true. If the condition is true, it will approach the roundabout, wait, enter it, and leave it in that order.

Next, the Stop subtree will execute its sequence in order and stop if any action fails. It will check whether Stop Ahead? is true. If the condition is true, it will approach the stop, wait, and go.

Next, the unnamed fallback will execute its children consecutively. If the inverted car-following branch fails, it will execute the lane-changing sequence. If the inverted car-following branch succeeds, it will stop without executing the lane-changing sequence.

Next, the inverter will execute the unnamed fallback and reverse its result. If the inner fallback succeeds, the inverter will fail. If the inner fallback fails, the inverter will succeed.

Next, the inner fallback will execute its children consecutively. If Not Slowed by Car in Front? is false, it will execute the Multi-Lane subtree and then the Single-Lane subtree if needed. If neither lane subtree succeeds, the fallback will fail.

Next, the Multi-Lane subtree will execute its fallback. The fallback will execute its sequence and fail if any child fails. It will check whether Multi-Lane? is true. It will check whether Left Lane available? is true. It will wait for the left lane to become free and switch to the left lane.

Next, the Single-Lane subtree will execute its sequence in order and stop if any action fails. It will check whether Single Lane with dotted Line? is true. It will wait for the left lane to become free and switch to the left lane. Its fallback will check whether Overtaking Possible is true. If overtaking is possible, it will overtake and switch to the right lane. If overtaking is not possible or the overtaking sequence fails, it will switch to the right lane.

Next, the lane-changing sequence will execute its children in order and stop if any child fails. It will check whether Right Lane Available? is true. It will check whether Not Slowed by Car in Front Right? is true. It will wait for the right lane to become free and switch to the right lane.

Finally, the Cruise action will execute if every preceding fallback branch fails.

Parameters: No action in this behavior tree has ports.

First, it will execute the Sequence actions (Print, Fallback, Fallback, Print) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

Next, it will execute the ROS action Print with the message “Hello”.

Then, it will execute the Fallback actions (Timeout, Sequence, Print) consecutively. If the Timeout action fails, it will move to the Sequence action. If the Sequence action fails, it will move to the ROS action Print. If no action succeeds, the execution will fail.

It will execute the Timeout action for the ROS action AlwaysRunning. If AlwaysRunning fails to execute within 2000 milliseconds, it will interrupt the execution and stop it.

If the ROS action AlwaysRunning succeeds within 2000 milliseconds, the fallback will succeed.

If the timeout action fails, it will execute the nested Sequence actions (ConditionCheck, Print) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

It will check whether the condition on topic “/condition” is true.

If the condition on topic “/condition” is true, it will execute the ROS action Print with the message “Baby”.

If the nested Sequence fails, it will execute the ROS action Print with the message “World”.

Next, it will execute the second Fallback actions (Sequence, Wait) consecutively. If the Sequence action fails, it will move to the ROS action Wait. If no action succeeds, the execution will fail.

It will execute the nested Sequence actions (MessageCheck, Trigger) in order and stop the sequence if any action fails.

It will check whether the message condition on topic “/trigger” is true.

If the message condition on topic “/trigger” is true, it will execute the ROS action Trigger using the “safety” service and a 100-millisecond connection timeout.

If the nested Sequence fails, it will execute the ROS action Wait for 3000 milliseconds.

Finally, it will execute the ROS action Print with the message “Done”.

  This Behavior Tree replans the global path periodically at 1 Hz and it also has
  recovery actions.

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="6" name="NavigateRecovery">
      <PipelineSequence name="NavigateWithReplanning">
        <RateController hz="1.0">
          <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="ComputePathToPose">
            <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
            <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Context" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
          </RecoveryNode>
        </RateController>
        <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="FollowPath">
          <FollowPath path="{path}" controller_id="FollowPath"/>
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap-Context" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
        </RecoveryNode>
      </PipelineSequence>
      <ReactiveFallback name="RecoveryFallback">
        <GoalUpdated/>
        <SequenceStar name="RecoveryActions">
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
          <Spin spin_dist="1.57"/>
          <Wait wait_duration="5"/>
        </SequenceStar>
      </ReactiveFallback>
    </RecoveryNode>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes navigation to a goal with periodic path replanning and recovery actions.

First, the root NavigateRecovery recovery node will execute the main navigation subtree. If the main navigation subtree fails, it will execute the RecoveryFallback recovery subtree and retry the main navigation subtree until six recovery attempts are exhausted.

Next, the NavigateWithReplanning pipeline sequence will execute RateController and FollowPath in order and stop if any action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action.

Next, the RateController decorator will run at a frequency of 1.0 hertz. It will execute the ComputePathToPose recovery node at that rate.

Next, the ComputePathToPose recovery node will execute the ROS action ComputePathToPose. If path computation fails, it will execute ClearGlobalCostmap-Context and retry path computation once.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath after path computation is running or succeeds. If path following fails, it will execute ClearLocalCostmap-Context and retry path following once.

Finally, the RecoveryFallback reactive fallback will execute GoalUpdated and RecoveryActions in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will execute and re-evaluate GoalUpdated whenever RecoveryActions is running. If GoalUpdated then succeeds, it will halt the running recovery actions and stop the fallback.

Next, the RecoveryActions sequence will execute ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree, ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree, Spin, and Wait in sequence. If any action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If any action fails, it will restart the sequence from that failed action.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive goal from {goal}, store its path under {path}, and use planner_id GridBased. The ROS action FollowPath will receive path from {path} and use controller_id FollowPath. ClearGlobalCostmap-Context will use service_name global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap. ClearLocalCostmap-Context will use service_name local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap. ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap. ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap. Spin will use spin_dist 1.57. Wait will use wait_duration 5.
