mrq:
The mission describes navigating to a goal while periodically replanning the global path and using recovery actions when navigation fails.

First, the root recovery node will execute the main navigation pipeline. If the main navigation pipeline fails, it will execute the recovery fallback and retry the main navigation pipeline. It will stop execution when recovery retries are exhausted.

Next, the pipeline sequence will execute the rate-controlled path computation and path following in order. It will advance to path following while path computation is running or has succeeded. It will stop if either action fails.

Next, the rate controller will run the path-computation recovery node at a frequency of 1.0 hertz.

Next, the path-computation recovery node will execute the path computation action. If it fails, it will clear the global costmap and retry path computation. It will stop if recovery fails after one retry.

Next, it will run the ROS action ComputePathToPose with the goal read from the blackboard and store the resulting path on the blackboard.

Next, the path-following recovery node will execute the path-following action. If it fails, it will clear the local costmap and retry path following. It will stop if recovery fails after one retry.

Next, it will run the ROS action FollowPath using the stored path.

Next, the recovery fallback will execute the goal-updated condition and the recovery-actions sequence in order. If the goal-updated condition succeeds, it will stop recovery processing. If the goal-updated condition fails, it will execute the recovery-actions sequence.

Next, the sequence with memory will execute the local costmap clearing, global costmap clearing, spinning, and waiting actions in order. If an action succeeds, it will remember that action and move to the next action. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action.

Next, it will clear the local costmap.

Next, it will clear the global costmap.

Next, it will spin by 1.57 radians.

Next, it will wait for 5 seconds.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will use goal="{goal}", path="{path}", and planner_id="GridBased". The ROS action FollowPath will use path="{path}" and controller_id="FollowPath". The ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearGlobalCostmap-Context will use service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap". The ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearLocalCostmap-Context will use service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap". The ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap". The ROS action ClearEntireCostmap named ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree will use service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap". The ROS action Spin will use spin_dist="1.57". The ROS action Wait will use wait_duration="5".

Next, ReactiveLTLStateCheck will check whether the current LTL state matches the desired sequence.

Next, ForceFailure will execute ReplanningRequestLevel2 and make sure it always fails.

Next, ForceFailure will execute ReplanningRequestLevel3 and make sure it always fails.

Next, the pipeline sequence NavigateWithReplanning will execute RateController and FollowPath in order and stop if either action fails. While RateController or FollowPath is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action.

Next, the rate controller will execute ComputePathToPose at a frequency of 1.0 hertz.

Next, the recovery node ComputePathToPose will execute main action ComputePathToPose. If it fails, it will execute recovery action PathToPoseFallback and retry ComputePathToPose. If PathToPoseFallback fails and four retries are exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, the custom action ComputePathToPose will compute a path to the goal with the GridBased planner.

Next, the reactive fallback PathToPoseFallback will execute GoalUpdated and GlobalPlannerRecoveryActions in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will execute GlobalPlannerRecoveryActions and re-evaluate GoalUpdated whenever the later action is running. If GoalUpdated then succeeds, it will halt the running recovery action and stop the fallback.

Next, the round-robin node GlobalPlannerRecoveryActions will execute ClearGlobalCostmap-Context and Wait as recovery actions in rotation.

Next, the custom action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context will clear the global costmap.

Next, the custom action Wait will wait for two seconds.

Next, the Repeat node will execute the custom action VariantAction continuously until it fails or succeeds. The custom action VariantAction will write the selected task variant to the blackboard key {variant}.

Then, the Switch3 node will read the blackboard value {variant} and compare it with the cases pick, deliver, and dock. If the value is pick, it will execute the PickDeliverCharge subtree. If the value is deliver, it will execute the DeliverCharge subtree. If the value is dock, it will execute the Charge subtree. If no case matches, it will execute the PickDeliverCharge subtree.

First, the PickDeliverCharge sequence will execute pick_subtree, Deliver, and GoTo in order and will stop if any action fails. It will execute the pick_subtree before delivery. It will execute the Deliver subtree before traveling to the charging coordinates.

Next, the pick_subtree sequence will execute objectplacement and Repeat in order and will stop if either action fails. It will execute the custom action objectplacement with the wooden box query. It will execute the Repeat node four times. The ForceSuccess decorator will execute the pick sequence and make sure it always succeeds. The pick sequence will execute TxtToWaypointsAction, GoTo, and objectplacement in order and will stop if any action fails. It will generate target coordinates for the boxes path. Next, AlarmTree will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will check Alarm and IsCivilian. It will execute AbortJob. It will try the first safe-room sequence before the second safe-room sequence. The first safe-room sequence will check IsInSafeRoom and then execute RandomMove. If that sequence fails, the second safe-room sequence will execute GetSafeRoomPosition and Move.

Next, Combat will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will try IsInCombat before HasHuntTarget. If both checks fail, Combat will fail. It will execute AbortJob. It will execute the target-engagement sequence and make sure that sequence always succeeds. That sequence will execute GetTarget, Move, and the adjacent-target sequence in order. The adjacent-target sequence will check TargetAdjacent and then execute AttackTarget. Combat will finally check IsInCombat.

Next, Mission will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will check IsOnMission. It will execute AbortJob, GetExitPosition, Move, LeaveForMission, DoMission, and ReturnFromMission in order.

Next, Needs will execute Hunger, Thirst, and Sleepy consecutively. If any subtree succeeds, it will stop. If every subtree fails, it will repeat the evaluation from Hunger until one succeeds.

Next, Hunger will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will check IsHungry. It will execute the Hunger sequence and then check IsFull. The Hunger sequence will execute FindFood, Move, PickUpItem, the dining sequence, and Eat in order. The dining sequence will execute FindDining and Move and will always succeed.

Next, Thirst will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will check IsThirsty. It will execute the Thirst sequence and then check IsDrinkFull. The Thirst sequence will execute FindDrink, Move, PickUpItem, the dining sequence, and Drink in order. The dining sequence will execute FindDining and Move and will always succeed.

Next, Sleepy will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will check IsSleepy. It will execute FindBed and Move and will always succeed. It will execute Sleep.

Next, GnomeStandard will execute its children consecutively. If any child succeeds, it will stop. If all children fail, it will repeat from the beginning until one succeeds. Its first child will retry GetUniform, PickUpBandages, Training, and Trainer from the beginning until one succeeds. If that child fails, it will try Jobs. If Jobs fails, it will execute RandomMove.

Next, GetUniform will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will execute CheckUniform. It will try Move before UniformCleanUp. It will execute EquipUniform after one of those actions succeeds.

Next, PickUpBandages will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will execute CheckBandages, Move, and PickUpItem in order.

Next, Training will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will check IsTrainingTime. It will execute FindTrainingGround, Move, and Train in order.

Next, Trainer will execute its children in sequence while remembering successful children. It will stop and restart from the failed child if any child fails. It will check IsTrainer. It will execute FindTrainerPosition, Move, and SuperviseTraining in order.

Next, Jobs will execute GetJob and then the job-selection fallback. The job-selection fallback will try each job subtree from left to right until one succeeds. If every job subtree fails, it will retry the complete list from the beginning until one succeeds.

Next, JobButcherAnimal will execute only when JobType matches ButcherAnimal. It will try the butcher-job sequence before AbortJob. The butcher-job sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ButcherAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If that sequence fails, it will execute AbortJob.

Next, JobDyeAnimal will execute only when JobType matches DyeAnimal. It will try the dye-job sequence before AbortJob. The dye-job sequence will execute InitJob, ClaimItems, MoveAllItemsToJob, InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, DyeAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If that sequence fails, it will execute AbortJob.

Next, JobLeadAnimalToPasture will execute only when JobType matches LeadAnimalToPasture. It will try the pasture-job sequence before AbortJob. The pasture-job sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If that sequence fails, it will execute AbortJob.

Next, JobHarvestAnimal will execute only when JobType matches HarvestAnimal. It will try the harvest-job sequence before AbortJob. The harvest-job sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, HarvestAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If that sequence fails, it will execute AbortJob.

Next, JobTameAnimal will execute only when JobType matches TameAnimal. It will try the tame-job sequence before AbortJob. The tame-job sequence will execute InitAnimalJob, Move, TameAnimal, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If that sequence fails, it will execute AbortJob.

Next, JobHaulMultiple will execute only when JobType matches HauleMultipleItems. It will try the hauling sequence before AbortJob. The hauling sequence will execute InitJob, FindTool, Move, and EquipTool in order. It will execute the item-pickup loop in inverted form. The item-pickup loop will continue while AllPickedUp is false, execute Move and PickUpItem, and continue running through ReturnAlwaysRunning. It will then check AllPickedUp. It will execute GetItemDropPosition, Move, DropAllItems, and FinishJob. If the hauling sequence fails, it will execute AbortJob.

The item-transfer loop will continue while AllItemsInPlaceForJob is false, execute Move, PickUpItem, GetItemDropPosition, Move, and DropItem, and continue running through ReturnAlwaysRunning. It will finally check AllItemsInPlaceForJob.

Next, OldMoveAllItemsToJob will try AllItemsInPlaceForJob before the transfer sequence. If the condition fails, it will retry the transfer sequence until it succeeds or reaches 20 attempts. The transfer sequence will execute the item-moving sequence and then check AllItemsInPlaceForJob. The item-moving sequence will execute Move and PickUpItem. It will try GetItemDropPosition before DropItem. It will try Move before DropItem. It will execute DropItem. If all attempts fail, it will execute AbortJob and make sure that action always fails.

Next, it will evaluate the SeeItem condition. The condition will succeed when it sees an item.

Next, it will execute the custom action Pick it up when the inverted See an Item condition fails.

Finally, it will execute the custom action Keep Running.

The mission describes a traffic-navigation behavior that waits when the mission is paused and otherwise selects lane keeping, lane changing, or A* navigation while checking traffic conditions and publishing data.

First, the root Fallback named Core_seq will execute its child sequences consecutively. If the first sequence fails, it will execute the second sequence. If either sequence succeeds, it will stop the fallback. If both sequences fail, the mission will fail.

Next, the first sequence will check whether checkMissionWait is true and will execute custom action stop when that condition succeeds. If checkMissionWait is false, this sequence will fail and the root fallback will continue.

Next, the second sequence will execute gen_path, traffic_check, and publishData in order. It will stop if any action fails.

Next, the gen_path sequence will check whether checkExistPathGlobal is true. It will execute custom action init after that condition succeeds. It will then use the StateSelect fallback to select a state-specific behavior. If the state-specific behavior fails, gen_path will fail.

Next, the StateSelect fallback will try LaneKeeping, LaneChangeLeft, LaneChangeRigth, Astar, and Recovery in order. If one child succeeds, it will stop. If all preceding children fail, it will try the next child. Recovery will always fail.

Next, the LaneKeeping sequence will check whether checkStateLaneKeeping is true. It will execute custom action genPathLaneKeeping and then custom action setPath. It will then use its fallback to select obstacle handling, global lane-change handling, or the default lane-keeping state. If all fallback branches fail, LaneKeeping will fail.

Next, the obstacle-handling fallback will first execute its front-object sequence. If that sequence fails, it will execute the lane_change fallback. If both branches fail, it will execute custom action setStateLaneKeeping.

Next, the front-object sequence will check whether checkFrontObject is true. It will then use the lane_keeping fallback to try the near-corner, near-stopline, and profitable-lane-keeping sequences. If all three sequences fail, it will try the lane_change fallback. It will then use the A* fallback, which will execute the astar sequence when possible and will otherwise execute AlwaysSuccess.

Next, the lane_keeping fallback will try the near-corner sequence first. That sequence will check whether checkNearCorner is true and will execute custom action acc. If it fails, the fallback will try the near-stopline sequence. If that fails, it will try the profitable-lane-keeping sequence.

Next, the lane_change fallback will try lane_change_left first. If that sequence fails, it will try lane_change_right. If both sequences fail, the fallback will fail.

Next, the lane_change_left sequence will execute custom action genPathLaneChangeLeft. It will check whether checkLaneChangeableLeft is true. It will then use a fallback to check collision handling before executing the lane-change branch. If checkCollision is true, it will execute custom action setStateLaneKeeping and custom action keepLane. Otherwise, it will execute custom action setStateLaneChangeLeft and custom action laneChangeLeft.

Next, the lane_change_right sequence will execute custom action genPathLaneChangeRight. It will check whether checkLaneChangeableRight is true. It will then use a fallback to check collision handling before executing the lane-change branch. If checkCollision is true, it will execute custom action setStateLaneKeeping and custom action keepLane. Otherwise, it will execute custom action setStateLaneChangeRight and custom action laneChangeRight.

Next, the astar sequence will check whether checkAbleAstar is true. It will then execute Gen_Local, which will stop the robot, set the A* state, and generate an A* path.

Next, the global lane-change sequence will check whether checkGlobalLaneChange is true. It will then use a fallback to try the left-change branch before the right-change branch. The left-change branch will check whether checkLeftChange is true, attempt to generate a left lane-change path, and check whether that path was generated. The right-change branch will attempt to generate a right lane-change path and will check whether that path was generated. Each successful lane-change path will use collision handling before either keeping the lane or changing lanes. The LaneKeeping sequence will then execute custom action setStateLaneKeeping.

Next, the LaneChangeLeft sequence will check whether checkStateLaneChangeLeft is true. It will execute custom action setPath. It will then use a fallback to check collision completion, lane-change completion, or continued left lane changing. It will set the state to lane keeping when checkCollision or checkEndLaneChange is true. Otherwise, it will execute custom action setStateLaneChangeLeft.

Next, the LaneChangeRigth sequence will check whether checkStateLaneChangeRight is true. It will execute custom action setPath. It will then use a fallback to check collision completion, lane-change completion, or continued right lane changing. It will set the state to lane keeping when checkCollision or checkEndLaneChange is true. Otherwise, it will execute custom action setStateLaneChangeRight.

Next, the Astar sequence will check whether checkStateAstar is true. It will execute custom action setPath. It will then use the local_check fallback to handle collision, A* completion, or local path following. If checkCollision is true, it will stop and generate another A* path. If checkFinishAstar is true, it will set the local path as finished and return to lane keeping. Otherwise, it will execute custom action localPathfollow.

Next, the traffic_check sequence will use a fallback to evaluate traffic-light passage and driving. If checkPassAbleTrafficLight is true, it will stop when checkCollision is true and will otherwise drive. If traffic passage is not allowed, it will execute custom action stopTrafficLight. If the traffic-light branch fails, it will execute custom action drive. It will then execute custom action setPath.

Finally, the second main sequence will execute custom action publishData after gen_path and traffic_check succeed.

Parameters: No action ports are defined in the behavior tree.

The mission describes following a dynamically updated goal to within a specified distance while periodically replanning the path.

First, the root PipelineSequence named NavigateWithReplanning will execute the RateController and KeepRunningUntilFailure in order and stop the sequence if any action fails. While an action is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next action.

Next, the RateController will execute its child sequence at a rate of 1.0 hertz. The child sequence will execute GoalUpdater and TruncatePath in order and stop if either action fails. The GoalUpdater will update the input goal before its child action runs. The ROS action ComputePathToPose will calculate a path to the updated goal. The TruncatePath action will shorten the calculated path to a distance of 1.0.

Finally, the KeepRunningUntilFailure decorator will execute the ROS action FollowPath. If the ROS action FollowPath succeeds, it will restart the action. If the ROS action FollowPath fails, it will stop looping and continue execution.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will read {updated_goal} through its goal port, store its result in {path} through its path port, and use GridBased through its planner_id port. The GoalUpdater action will read {goal} through its input_goal port and store the updated goal in {updated_goal} through its output_goal port. The RateController decorator will use 1.0 through its hz port. The TruncatePath action will use 1.0 through its distance port, read {path} through its input_path port, and store the shortened path in {truncated_path} through its output_path port. The ROS action FollowPath will read {truncated_path} through its path port and use FollowPath through its controller_id port.

Then, the RecoveryNode named ComputePathToPose will execute main ComputePathToPose. If it fails, it will execute ComputePathToPoseRecoveryFallback. After recovery, it will retry ComputePathToPose. If recovery fails and one retry is exhausted, it will stop execution.

Next, the ReactiveFallback named ComputePathToPoseRecoveryFallback will execute GoalUpdated and ClearGlobalCostmap-Context in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. If it fails, it will execute and re-evaluate ClearGlobalCostmap-Context until an action succeeds.

Then, the DistanceController will execute SmoothPath after the required distance condition and stop if the action fails.

Next, the RecoveryNode named SmoothPath will execute main SmoothPath. If it fails, it will execute SmoothPathRecoveryFallback. After recovery, it will retry SmoothPath. If recovery fails and one retry is exhausted, it will stop execution.

Then, the ReactiveFallback named SmoothPathRecoveryFallback will execute GoalUpdated and the clearing sequence in order. If GoalUpdated succeeds, it will stop execution. If it fails, it will execute and re-evaluate the clearing sequence until an action succeeds.

mrq:
The mission describes a gripping task that monitors the left suction cup and then configures the gripper through a sequence of suction-cup checks.

First, the root sequence will execute the ReactiveFallback subtree and then the second sequence in order. It will stop the root sequence if either subtree fails.

Next, the ReactiveFallback will execute the ReactiveSequence and the Pince action in order until one child succeeds. If a child fails, it will move to the next child. If both children fail, the fallback will fail. While a child is running, it will re-evaluate earlier children, and it will stop the running child if an earlier child succeeds.

Next, the ReactiveSequence will execute the inverted IsVentouseGauche condition and the Attendre action in sequence. If either child fails, it will stop execution. While Attendre is running, it will re-evaluate the inverted condition and halt the wait if that condition fails.

Next, the Inverter will execute the IsVentouseGauche condition with its result reversed. If IsVentouseGauche succeeds, the inverter will fail. If IsVentouseGauche fails, the inverter will succeed.

Next, it will execute the ROS action Attendre after its delay timer expires. The delay will be 3000 milliseconds.

Next, it will execute the custom action Pince if the ReactiveSequence fails. The action will open the left valve while keeping the middle and right valves closed.

Next, the second sequence will execute IsVentouseGauche, Pince, IsVentouseCentre, Pince, IsVentouseDroite, and Pince in order. It will stop if any condition or action fails.

Next, it will check whether IsVentouseGauche is true. It will execute the custom action Pince after that condition succeeds. The action will open the left valve while keeping the middle and right valves closed.

Next, it will check whether IsVentouseCentre is true. It will execute the custom action Pince after that condition succeeds. The action will open the middle valve while keeping the left and right valves closed.

Next, it will check whether IsVentouseDroite is true. It will execute the custom action Pince after that condition succeeds. The action will open the right valve while keeping the middle and left valves closed.

Parameters: The Attendre action will receive ms=3000. The first Pince action will receive middle_valve=false, right_valve=false, and left_valve=true. The second Pince action will receive middle_valve=true, right_valve=false, and left_valve=false. The third Pince action will receive middle_valve=false, right_valve=true, and left_valve=false.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree replans the global path periodically at 1 Hz through an array of poses continuously
   and it also has recovery actions specific to planning / control as well as general system issues.
-->
<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="6" name="NavigateRecovery">
      <PipelineSequence name="NavigateWithReplanning">
        <RateController hz="0.333">
          <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="ComputePathThroughPoses">
            <ReactiveSequence>
              <RemovePassedGoals input_goals="{goals}" output_goals="{goals}" radius="0.5"/>
              <ComputePathThroughPoses goals="{goals}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
            </ReactiveSequence>
            <ReactiveFallback name="ComputePathThroughPosesRecoveryFallback">
              <GoalUpdated/>
              <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Context" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
            </ReactiveFallback>
          </RecoveryNode>
        </RateController>
        <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="FollowPath">
          <FollowPath path="{path}" controller_id="FollowPath"/>
          <ReactiveFallback name="FollowPathRecoveryFallback">
            <GoalUpdated/>
            <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap-Context" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
          </ReactiveFallback>
        </RecoveryNode>
      </PipelineSequence>
      <ReactiveFallback name="RecoveryFallback">
        <GoalUpdated/>
        <RoundRobin name="RecoveryActions">
          <Sequence name="ClearingActions">
            <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
            <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Subtree" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
          </Sequence>
          <Spin spin_dist="1.57"/>
          <Wait wait_duration="5"/>
          <BackUp backup_dist="0.15" backup_speed="0.025"/>
        </RoundRobin>
      </ReactiveFallback>
    </RecoveryNode>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes navigating through an array of poses while periodically replanning the global path and applying planning, control, and system recovery actions.

First, the root recovery node will execute the main navigation pipeline. If the main navigation pipeline fails, it will execute the recovery fallback and retry the main navigation pipeline until the configured retries are exhausted.

Next, the pipeline sequence will execute the replanning branch and the path-following branch in order. While either branch is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to the next branch. The pipeline will stop if either branch fails.

Next, the rate controller will limit the path-planning branch to 0.333 Hz. It will execute the path-planning recovery node at that rate.

Next, the path-planning recovery node will execute the reactive planning sequence. If the planning sequence fails, it will execute the planning recovery fallback and retry the planning sequence until its retry is exhausted.

Next, the reactive planning sequence will execute RemovePassedGoals and ComputePathThroughPoses in order. While ComputePathThroughPoses is running, it will re-evaluate RemovePassedGoals. If either action fails, it will stop the sequence.

Next, it will run the custom action RemovePassedGoals with the current goals, remove goals within the configured radius, and store the remaining goals under {goals}. It will then run the ROS action ComputePathThroughPoses with {goals} and store the resulting path under {path}.

Next, the planning recovery fallback will execute GoalUpdated and ClearGlobalCostmap-Context in order until one action succeeds. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate previous actions. If an earlier action succeeds, it will stop the running action.

Next, it will check whether GoalUpdated is true. If that check fails, it will run the ROS action ClearGlobalCostmap-Context to clear the global costmap.

Next, the path-following recovery node will execute the ROS action FollowPath. If FollowPath fails, it will execute the path-following recovery fallback and retry FollowPath until its retry is exhausted.

Next, the path-following recovery fallback will execute GoalUpdated and ClearLocalCostmap-Context in order until one action succeeds. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate previous actions. If an earlier action succeeds, it will stop the running action.

Next, it will check whether GoalUpdated is true. If that check fails, it will run the ROS action ClearLocalCostmap-Context to clear the local costmap.

Finally, the system recovery fallback will execute GoalUpdated and RecoveryActions in order until one action succeeds. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate previous actions. If an earlier action succeeds, it will stop the running action.

Finally, it will check whether GoalUpdated is true. If that check fails, it will execute RecoveryActions.

Finally, the round-robin recovery action will select and execute its child recovery action in rotation.

The mission describes a robot that responds to alarms, combat, missions, personal needs, training, supplies, and assigned jobs.

First, the root fallback will execute AlarmTree, Combat, Mission, Needs, and GnomeStandard consecutively. If any subtree succeeds, it will stop. If a subtree fails, it will continue to the next subtree. If every subtree fails, the root fallback will fail.

Next, AlarmTree will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will check whether Alarm is true. It will check whether IsCivilian is true. It will abort the current job. It will use the fallback to try the safe-room sequence before the alternate safe-room sequence. The safe-room sequence will check whether IsInSafeRoom is true and will perform RandomMove. If that sequence fails, the alternate sequence will perform GetSafeRoomPosition and Move.

Next, Combat will use the fallback to check IsInCombat and then HasHuntTarget. It will abort the current job after either check succeeds. It will execute the forced-success combat sequence, which will always succeed regardless of its child result. That sequence will perform GetTarget, Move, and the nested sequence. The nested sequence will check TargetAdjacent and will perform AttackTarget if the check succeeds. Combat will finally check whether IsInCombat is true.

Next, Mission will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will check whether IsOnMission is true. It will abort the current job. It will perform GetExitPosition, Move, LeaveForMission, DoMission, and ReturnFromMission.

Next, the Needs fallback named Needs will try Hunger, Thirst, and Sleepy consecutively. If any subtree succeeds, it will stop. If all subtrees fail, it will retry from Hunger until one subtree succeeds.

Next, Hunger will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will check whether IsHungry is true. It will execute the nested sequence, which will perform FindFood, Move, PickUpItem, and the forced-success dining sequence. The dining sequence will always succeed and will perform FindDining and Move. Hunger will then check whether IsFull is true.

Next, Thirst will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will check whether IsThirsty is true. It will execute the nested sequence, which will perform FindDrink, Move, PickUpItem, and the forced-success dining sequence. The dining sequence will always succeed and will perform FindDining and Move. Thirst will then check whether IsDrinkFull is true.

Next, Sleepy will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will check whether IsSleepy is true. It will execute the forced-success sleeping-location sequence, which will always succeed and will perform FindBed and Move. It will then perform Sleep.

Next, GnomeStandard will use its fallback to try the nested fallback, Jobs, and RandomMove consecutively. If an action succeeds, it will stop. If all actions fail, it will retry from the nested fallback until one action succeeds. The nested fallback will retry PickUpBandages, Training, and Trainer from the beginning until one succeeds.

Next, PickUpBandages will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will perform CheckBandages, Move, and PickUpItem.

Next, Training will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will check whether IsTrainingTime is true. It will perform FindTrainingGround, Move, and Train.

Next, Trainer will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will check whether IsTrainer is true. It will perform FindTrainerPosition, Move, and SuperviseTraining.

Next, Jobs will execute its actions in sequence and remember each successful action. It will use the fallback to try CheckUniform and then GetJob. If the first action fails, it will execute the second action. It will then use the fallback-star to try JobButcherAnimal, JobDyeAnimal, JobLeadAnimalToPasture, JobHarvestAnimal, JobTameAnimal, JobHaulMultiple, and JobStandard. If a job subtree fails, it will try the next subtree. If every job subtree fails, it will restart from JobButcherAnimal.

Next, JobButcherAnimal will check whether the blackboard value JobType matches ButcherAnimal. If the precondition is satisfied, it will use the fallback to try the job sequence and then AbortJob. The job sequence will perform InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ButcherAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If the job sequence fails, it will abort the job.

Next, JobDyeAnimal will check whether JobType matches DyeAnimal. If the precondition is satisfied, it will use the fallback to try the job sequence and then AbortJob. The job sequence will perform InitJob, ClaimItems, MoveAllItemsToJob, InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, DyeAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If the job sequence fails, it will abort the job.

Next, JobLeadAnimalToPasture will check whether JobType matches LeadAnimalToPasture. If the precondition is satisfied, it will use the fallback to try the job sequence and then AbortJob. The job sequence will perform InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If the job sequence fails, it will abort the job.

Next, JobHarvestAnimal will check whether JobType matches HarvestAnimal. If the precondition is satisfied, it will use the fallback to try the job sequence and then AbortJob. The job sequence will perform InitAnimalJob, Move, GrabAnimal, HarvestAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If the job sequence fails, it will abort the job.

Next, JobTameAnimal will check whether JobType matches TameAnimal. If the precondition is satisfied, it will use the fallback to try the job sequence and then AbortJob. The job sequence will perform InitAnimalJob, Move, TameAnimal, GrabAnimal, GetItemDropPosition, Move, FinalMoveAnimal, ReleaseAnimal, and FinishJob in order. If the job sequence fails, it will abort the job.

Next, JobHaulMultiple will check whether JobType matches HauleMultipleItems. If the precondition is satisfied, it will use the fallback to try the job sequence and then AbortJob. The job sequence will perform InitJob, FindTool, Move, and EquipTool. It will execute the inverted item-collection sequence. The inner sequence will invert the AllPickedUp check, perform Move and PickUpItem, and execute ReturnAlwaysRunning. The outer inverter will reverse the result of that sequence. The job sequence will then check whether AllPickedUp is true. It will perform GetItemDropPosition, Move, DropAllItems, and FinishJob. If the job sequence fails, it will abort the job.

Next, JobStandard will use the fallback to try the named StandardJobs sequence and then AbortJob. The StandardJobs sequence will perform InitJob, ClaimItems, FindTool, Move, EquipTool, MoveAllItemsToJob, GetWorkPosition, Move, Work, and FinishJob in order. If the standard job sequence fails, it will abort the job.

Next, MoveAllItemsToJob will execute its actions in order and stop if an action fails. It will execute the inverted item-transfer sequence. The inner sequence will invert the AllItemsInPlaceForJob check, perform Move, PickUpItem, GetItemDropPosition, Move, DropItem, and execute ReturnAlwaysRunning. The outer inverter will reverse the result of that sequence. It will then check whether AllItemsInPlaceForJob is true.

Next, OldMoveAllItemsToJob will use the fallback-star to try the completion check, the retry sequence, and the forced-failure recovery action. If the completion check fails, it will retry the item-transfer sequence up to 20 attempts until the sequence succeeds. The item-transfer sequence will perform Move, PickUpItem, and the first fallback. The first fallback will try GetItemDropPosition and then DropItem. The second fallback will try Move and then DropItem. The sequence will perform DropItem again and will check whether AllItemsInPlaceForJob is true. If all attempts fail, the forced-failure action will perform AbortJob and will always fail. If every fallback option fails, the fallback-star will restart from the completion check.

Parameters: The BB_Precondition nodes will read JobType and compare it with ButcherAnimal, DyeAnimal, LeadAnimalToPasture, HarvestAnimal, TameAnimal, or HauleMultipleItems as specified. The RetryUntilSuccesful node will use num_attempts set to 20.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first computes a path using the global planner (ComputePathToPose).
  Then, it runs two sub-branches in parallel. The first sub-branch is a FollowPath
  operation (the local planner). In parallel, there is a rate controlled execution of
  FollowPath (the global planner). Each time a new path is computed, the path update
  is sent to the local planner. The right branch, which is the rate controlled
  ComputePathToPose, always returns RUNNING. Because the Parallel node uses a
  threshold of 1, whenever the FollowPath returns SUCCESS or FAILURE, the parallel
  node will return this result.

  The goal (input to the global planner) and the resulting path (output of the global
  planner and input to the local planner) are passed on the blackboard.

  The rate at which the ComputePathToPose operation is invoked can be controlled with
  the hz parameter to the RateController node.
-->

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <SequenceStar name="root">
      <ComputePathToPose goal="${goal}" path="${path}"/>
      <ParallelNode threshold="1">
        <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
        <Sequence>
          <RateController hz="1.0">
            <ComputePathToPose goal="${goal}" path="${path}"/>
          </RateController>
          <UpdatePath/>
        </Sequence>
      </ParallelNode>
    </SequenceStar>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Next, the ParallelNode will execute FollowPath and the second Sequence simultaneously. The parallel execution will succeed when one child succeeds. The parallel execution will fail when any child fails.

Next, it will execute the ROS action FollowPath using the current path from the blackboard. The action will determine the navigation result for the parallel execution.

Finally, the second Sequence will execute RateController and UpdatePath in order and stop if either action fails. While RateController is running or has succeeded, it will proceed to UpdatePath.

Next, the RateController will execute ComputePathToPose at a rate of 1.0 hertz. It will compute updated paths using the goal from the blackboard and store each result in the path entry.

Finally, it will execute UpdatePath after each rate-controlled path computation.

Parameters: The ROS action ComputePathToPose will receive goal={goal} and store its result under path={path}. The ROS action FollowPath will receive path={path}. The RateController will use hz=1.0.

Otherwise, it will continue executing and re-evaluating AllGoalsAchieved whenever the later action is running. If AllGoalsAchieved becomes true, it will halt the running action and stop the fallback.

Next, the KeepRunningUntilFailure node will execute the ReactiveSequence. If the ReactiveSequence succeeds, it will restart it. If the ReactiveSequence fails, it will stop looping and continue execution.

Then, the ReactiveSequence will execute GetNextGoal, ForceSuccess, and SetBlackboard in sequence. If an action fails, it will stop execution. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate previous actions. If a previous action fails during this re-evaluation, it will halt the running action and stop the sequence.

Next, it will execute the custom action GetNextGoal to select the next goal from the goals and update the goal-achieved state.

Then, the ForceSuccess node will execute NavigateToPose and make sure it always succeeds. It will execute the ROS action NavigateToPose using the selected goal. A failed navigation attempt will therefore not prevent the next action from running.

Finally, it will execute the custom action SetBlackboard to mark the current goal as achieved.

<!--
  This Behavior Tree first goes into a branch where it will check to see if the robot's initial
  pose is given. If the initial pose is not given it trys to automatically localize the robot.
  After finding the initial pose it will continue with the recovery and navigation branch.  The
  AutoLocalization branch is based on 'AutoLocalization.xml' and the navigation branch is based on
  `parallel_w_recovery.xml`.
-->
<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Sequence name="root">
      <FallbackStar name="AutoLocalization">
        <initialPoseReceived/>
        <SequenceStar name="doSelfLocalization">
          <RetryUntilSuccesful num_attempts="5" name="retry_client_request">
            <globalLocalizationServiceRequest/>
         </RetryUntilSuccesful>
         <RetryUntilSuccesful num_attempts="10" name="retry_localization">
            <Sequence>
              <Fallback>
                <IsLocalized/>
                <SequenceStar>
                 <Spin/>
                <BackUp/>
                 <Spin/>
              </SequenceStar>
             </Fallback>
             <IsLocalized/>
            </Sequence> 
          </RetryUntilSuccesful>
        </SequenceStar>
      </FallbackStar>
      <FallbackStar name="check_motion">
        <Inverter name="is_not_stuck">
          <IsStuck/>
        </Inverter>
        <SequenceStar name="stuck_recovery">
          <Stop/>
          <BackUp/>
          <Spin/>
        </SequenceStar>
      </FallbackStar>
      <SequenceStar name="navigate">
        <ComputePathToPose endpoints="${endpoints}" path="${path}"/>
        <ParallelNode threshold="1">
          <FollowPath path="${path}"/>
          <Sequence>
            <RateController hz="2">
              <ComputePathToPose endpoints="${endpoints}" path="${path}"/>
            </RateController>
            <UpdatePath/>
          </Sequence>
        </ParallelNode>
      </SequenceStar>
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes a robot localization, motion-recovery, and navigation task.

First, the root sequence will execute AutoLocalization, check_motion, and navigate in order and will stop if any action fails.

Next, the AutoLocalization fallback will consecutively execute initialPoseReceived and doSelfLocalization. If either action fails, it will move to the next action until one succeeds. If all actions fail, it will restart from initialPoseReceived until one succeeds. The initialPoseReceived condition will check whether an initial pose has been received. The doSelfLocalization sequence will execute retry_client_request and retry_localization in sequence while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. The retry_client_request retry node will keep trying globalLocalizationServiceRequest until it succeeds. The retry_localization retry node will keep trying its localization sequence until it succeeds. Its localization sequence will execute the first fallback and IsLocalized in order and will stop if an action fails. The first fallback will execute IsLocalized and the unnamed recovery sequence consecutively. If IsLocalized fails, it will execute the recovery sequence. If both actions fail, the fallback will fail. The recovery sequence will execute Spin, BackUp, and Spin in order and will stop if any action fails. The IsLocalized condition will check whether the robot is localized.

Next, the check_motion fallback will consecutively execute is_not_stuck and stuck_recovery. If either action fails, it will move to the next action until one succeeds. If all actions fail, it will restart from is_not_stuck until one succeeds. The is_not_stuck inverter will execute IsStuck with its result reversed. If IsStuck succeeds, the inverter will fail. If IsStuck fails, the inverter will succeed. The stuck_recovery sequence will execute Stop, BackUp, and Spin in order while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. The IsStuck condition will check whether the robot is stuck.

Finally, the navigate sequence will execute ComputePathToPose and the parallel navigation node in sequence while remembering successful actions. If an action fails, it will restart from that failed action. The parallel navigation node will execute FollowPath and its path-update sequence simultaneously. If at least one action succeeds, the parallel execution will succeed. If any action fails, the parallel execution will fail. The path-update sequence will execute RateController and UpdatePath in order and will stop if any action fails. The RateController will run its child at 2 Hz. Its child will execute ComputePathToPose. The FollowPath action will follow the stored path. The UpdatePath action will update the navigation path.

Parameters: ComputePathToPose will use endpoints from {endpoints} and store the path in {path}. globalLocalizationServiceRequest will use no ports. Spin will use no ports. BackUp will use no ports. Stop will use no ports. FollowPath will use the path from {path}. RateController will use a frequency of 2 Hz. UpdatePath will use no ports.

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <ReactiveFallback name="FollowWaypoints">
      <AllGoalsAchieved goal_achieved="{goal_achieved}"/>
      <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
        <ReactiveSequence>
          <GetNextGoal goals="{goals}" goal="{goal}" goal_achieved="{goal_achieved}"/>
          <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1">
            <NavigateToPose goal="{goal}"/>
            <Wait wait_duration="5"/>
          </RecoveryNode>
          <SetBlackboard output_key="goal_achieved" value="true"/>
        </ReactiveSequence>
      </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    </ReactiveFallback>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>
mrq:
The mission describes processing waypoints by navigating to each goal, waiting after navigation failure, and stopping when all goals are achieved.

First, the root ReactiveFallback named FollowWaypoints will execute AllGoalsAchieved and the KeepRunningUntilFailure subtree in order. If AllGoalsAchieved succeeds, it will stop execution. Otherwise, it will execute and re-evaluate the KeepRunningUntilFailure subtree until AllGoalsAchieved succeeds.

Next, the AllGoalsAchieved condition will check whether {goal_achieved} indicates that all goals have been achieved.

Next, the KeepRunningUntilFailure node will execute the ReactiveSequence. If the ReactiveSequence succeeds, it will restart the sequence. If the ReactiveSequence fails, it will stop looping and continue execution.

Next, the ReactiveSequence will execute GetNextGoal, the RecoveryNode, and SetBlackboard in sequence. If any action fails, it will stop execution. While a later action is running, it will re-evaluate the preceding actions and halt the running action if a preceding action fails.

Next, the GetNextGoal action will select the next goal from {goals} and store it in {goal}. It will use {goal_achieved} while selecting the next goal.

Next, the RecoveryNode will execute NavigateToPose as its main action. If NavigateToPose fails, it will execute Wait as the recovery action. After recovery, it will retry NavigateToPose. It will stop execution if the recovery action fails and the retry limit is exhausted.

Next, the Wait action will wait for five seconds before returning its result.

Next, the NavigateToPose action will navigate to the selected goal. After successful navigation, the SetBlackboard action will store true under {goal_achieved}.

Parameters: The NavigateToPose action will receive goal={goal}. The GetNextGoal action will receive goals={goals}, goal={goal}, and goal_achieved={goal_achieved}. The SetBlackboard action will receive output_key=goal_achieved and value=true. The Wait action will receive wait_duration=5.

The mission describes continuously pursuing goals by placing a held item or picking up a visible item.

First, the root Repeat node will execute the Fallback node named Pursue Goals indefinitely.

Next, the Fallback node named Pursue Goals will execute the Sequence node named Place Item followed by the Sequence node named Remove Item until one sequence succeeds. If both sequences fail, it will start again from Place Item.

The Sequence node named Place Item will execute the HoldingItem condition followed by the Place action in order and will stop if either child fails.

The HoldingItem condition will check whether the robot is holding an item.

The robot will execute the Place action if the HoldingItem condition succeeds.

The Sequence node named Remove Item will execute the SeeItem condition followed by the Pick action in order and will stop if either child fails.

The SeeItem condition will check whether it can see an item.

It will execute the Pick action if the SeeItem condition succeeds.

Parameters: The Place action has no declared ports. The Pick action has no declared ports.

Next, the PickAllPurpleAtoms sequence will move 652 units ahead, turn left by 90 degrees, move 145 units backward, and adjust by -1 degree.

It will execute each parallel movement and barrel-turning operation simultaneously and will succeed only when both child actions succeed.

It will move 100 units backward while setting barrelGoalPosition to 9535 and turning the barrel to that position.

It will execute PickAtomRight after the first barrel operation.

It will execute PickAtomRight after the fourth barrel operation.

It will move 100 units backward while setting barrelGoalPosition to 47675 and turning the barrel to that position.

It will execute PickAtomRight after the fifth barrel operation.

It will move 720 units ahead while setting barrelGoalPosition to 57230 and turning the barrel to that position.

It will execute PickAtomRight after the sixth barrel operation.

It will turn 182 degrees and move 1020 units ahead.

Next, the PickAtomRight sequence will move the arm front joint to position 950, move the arm side joint to position 235, and turn the arm to position 820.

It will move the arm side joint to position 1023 and wait 1500 milliseconds for the atom to be secured.

It will move the arm side joint back to position 235, turn the arm to position 510, and move the arm front joint to position 460.

It will wait 1000 milliseconds for the atom to fall, move the arm front joint to position 950, and wait another 500 milliseconds.

Next, the TurnBarrel sequence will activate the barrel, repeatedly check whether the barrel has reached barrelGoalPosition until the check succeeds, and deactivate the barrel.

The retry operation will attempt the barrel-position check until it succeeds.

Next, the EmptyBarrelLeft sequence will set barrelGoalPosition to 58360, turn the barrel to that position, and push the left atom outward and back.

It will set barrelGoalPosition to 96690, turn the barrel to that position, and push the left atom outward and back.

It will set barrelGoalPosition to 106320, turn the barrel to that position, and push the left atom outward and back.

Next, it will execute the custom action NoAmmo. If NoAmmo fails, it will execute the Sequence named fight_back.

Next, it will execute the custom action LowHP. After LowHP succeeds, it will execute the custom action Track. After Track succeeds, it will execute the custom action Attack.
